declared_source_paths: corpus/rhetorical_ontology/Heidegger, Martin - Being and Time_(1962)_[My Copy].pdf
provenance.notes: Declared in TWO places and both agree: bt-structured/manifest.json:4 `"source_pdf"` and bt-analysis/phase0-overview.md:4. File exists, 12,932,629 bytes. The PDF offset is declared (+1), justified against a concrete landmark (phase0-overview.md:5 'English p.21 (§1 heading) = PDF p.22'), and is consistent with every per-section pdf_pages value in the 17 bt-structured unit files. This is the strongest provenance in the batch and it is machine-readable. What is missing is span-level provenance: no unit or claim carries a character offset, bbox, or verified-quotation flag.

entries.granularity_gap: The FINEST unit the entry ENCODES in a structured slot is the section (§1-§83, 83 records in bt-structured with heading, H./eng/pdf page ranges, tags, german_terms_expected). Everything above section level is well covered; nothing below it is encoded in any machine-readable slot. BUT claim-level material is ALREADY AUTHORED and merely trapped in prose: 108 claim records exist as markdown table rows with a five-field schema (`| id | claim | premises | targets | status |`, ids BT-D1-U2-P1 style, status drawn from a 7-value vocabulary), each averaging one full claim sentence plus 3-6 enumerated premises plus an explicit list of what the claim argues against. On top of that, 299 typed edge objects sit in fenced JSON, ~86 tension items carry [INTERP-low/high] confidence tags AND explicit `Linked to: BT-D1-U2-P2` claim-level back-references (84 such links), and ~360 German-term table rows carry per-term h_pages. So claim-level is roughly 90% of the way there in content and 0% of the way there in form — the conversion is a parse job, not an analysis job. Clause-level is entirely absent: no sentence or clause is ever addressed, no quotation carries a span, and 1,230 quoted strings sit inline with only 37 locally cited. To reach the stated target one would need (a) a JSON schema for the existing 108 claims + 84 claim-to-tension links, (b) a verbatim layer anchoring each of the 1,230 quotations to H-page and character span, and (c) a clause decomposition of the premises fields, which are already semi-decomposed as numbered '(1)…(2)…(3)' lists and could be split mechanically.
strengths: Segmentation layer is exact and verifiable: all 17 bt-structured unit files agree with manifest.json on unit_id, file name, label, chapter and division; section counts per unit match the manifest's §-ranges in 17/17 cases; total sections in unit files == 83 == manifest total_sections; §§1-83 is fully covered with no section-level gaps or duplicates.
Source provenance is real and double-declared, the PDF exists, and the +1 offset is justified against a named landmark and consistent with all 83 per-section pdf_pages values.

The concept-matrix.csv is genuinely trustworthy: all 37 canonical_name values match the ontology exactly, centrality agrees in 37/37, and unit coverage agrees in 36/37 (the one exception is the ontology writing 'all 17 units' as prose).
The 108 claim records are a real asset — id, claim, enumerated premises, explicit targets/opponents, and a 7-value status vocabulary, consistently formatted across all 17 units.
The 84 `Linked to: BT-D1-U2-Pn` back-references from tension items to specific claims are exactly the claim-level connective tissue the programme needs, and they already exist.

bt-german-appendix.json is 300 lemmas with forms_encountered, key_sections, h_pages, units, translation_contested (63 flagged) and translator notes — a genuinely dissertation-grade terminological apparatus, and its declared count (300) matches the .md twin's header exactly.
phase0-overview.md's self-declared counts are all correct (38 provisional concepts = 38 table rows; 10 claims; 6 tensions) — the only file in the entry whose declared counts survive audit.
The edge relation vocabulary in global-edges.csv is genuinely controlled: 11 values, all lowercase snake_case, no free-text drift across 284 rows.
entries.verdict: Salvageable, and the most salvageable structure in the batch — but the runtime artifact it currently produces must be treated as broken. The authored substrate is strong: an exact 83-section segmentation, a verified PDF and offset, a 37-node ontology whose centralities and unit coverage are internally consistent, a 300-lemma German appendix, and — critically — 108 claim records with premises and targets that already sit one parse away from the user's claim-level target. Against its own stated standard (the manifest's quality_checks) it FAILS: two of five assertions are provably false, and the ontology file's last node plus the last node of each tier are corrupted at compile time into 586-element unit arrays and 247-character tier strings. Against the claim/clause-level target it is structurally INCAPABLE as currently wired — not because the analysis is too coarse, but because the pipeline reads only one of 53 files and that one file is the only place the claims are NOT stored. The right move is not a rebuild but a re-wire plus three surgical fixes: (1) fix the header-section parser's unreachable break and re-bound node parsing to §3A, which alone repairs 3 corrupted nodes; (2) lift the 108 claim tables and 299 fenced-JSON edges out of the prose into typed records, normalising the BT-/unprefixed unit-ID split; (3) resolve the 266 dangling CONCEPT: links in the German appendix. Rebuilding from scratch would destroy an exact, human-verified segmentation and 62,700 words of analysis that no automated pass will reproduce.

150 claim records with premises, an explicit conclusion step, and an 'Aristotelian texts' locus field — the locus field is something BT lacks entirely and is exactly what a citation-network layer would need.

bcap-greek-appendix.json is a serious apparatus: 67 lemmas with forms_encountered, conventional_translations, a substantive heidegger_usage gloss, key_aristotelian_loci (e.g. 7 loci for λόγος), and a per-unit translation_status map — a genuinely claim-level assertion set that is already machine-readable and already unit-scoped.

tension-edges.json is the better of the two sibling schemas: it carries id, label, units and productive_character, so its 7 edges reach compiled-index.json WITH unit provenance (BT's 9 reach it with units: []).
Section 3A's centrality criterion is stated explicitly and falsifiably (':11 core = appears in 5+ units AND has 10+ edges'), which is what makes the dedup override detectable at all.
The 20-edge bcap-graph-bridge.mmd is the only place in either entry where BT<->BCAP bridges are actually populated rather than stubbed out.
entries.verdict: Salvageable but needs heavier normalisation than its sibling, and its published statistics must be treated as untrustworthy. The intellectual content is excellent and in places the best in the batch — a subsection-level segmentation with Greek headings, 150 claim records carrying Aristotelian loci, a 67-lemma appendix with per-unit translation status, exact pdf offsets, and the only populated cross-text bridge. Against its own stated standard it FAILS hard: §3B declares an edge total and full relation/domain distributions that are wrong in every single line (87 vs 93 rows, all ten relation counts wrong, 5 phantom 'historicizes' edges), it declares a 10-value controlled relation vocabulary and then uses 79, it splits its concepts across three irreconcilable naming systems (Greek script / Latin transliteration / German-English), it leaves 5 of 13 units with no machine-readable edges including its second-largest analysis, and it ships one syntactically invalid JSON fence. Against the claim/clause-level target it is structurally incapable as wired — 98.3% of its authored bytes never reach the compiler, and the 1.7% that does gets its centrality overwritten on 9 of 37 nodes and its definitions on 15, because 17 of its node names collide by lowercased key with Aristotle's. I would NOT rebuild it: the 84,000 words of analysis, the subsection segmentation and the Greek appendix are irreplaceable. I WOULD treat every count it publishes about itself as unverified until recomputed, normalise the naming to Greek-script-with-transliteration-alias, unify the 79 relations onto the declared 10, backfill edges for the 5 empty units, and give the ontology a text-qualified node key so Aristotle stops eating it.

result.batch_notes:
CROSS-ENTRY OBSERVATIONS

1. Same layout family, incompatible serializations. Both entries are structured/analysis pairs built days apart (BCAP 2026-03-08, BT 2026-03-09) by the same template, yet: global-edges.csv column ORDER differs (BT `source,target,relation,edge_domain,units,note`; BCAP `source,relation,target,edge_domain,note,units` — same six names, different positions, so any positional reader silently swaps relation and target); concept-matrix headers differ (BT `canonical_name,german_lemma,centrality,…`; BCAP `Concept,Greek,…,Total`); tension-edges.json schemas differ (BT lacks id/label/units, BCAP has all three); unit-record schemas differ (BT `label`+`division`, no unit-level page range; BCAP `title`+`pages`+`pdf_pages`, no division); per-unit edge objects differ (BT `{source,target,relation,edge_domain,note}` with CONCEPT:/POSITION:/TRADITION:/INTERLOCUTOR:/UNIT: prefixes; BCAP `{source,target,relation,label}` with bare transliterated ids); ontology_format differs (header vs table) even though both files are called book-level-ontology.md. Two entries, ~9 dialect divergences.

2. THE BIG FINDING — claim-level material already exists, unstructured. 258 claim records across the batch (BT 108, BCAP 150), each with a claim sentence, enumerated premises, and a status/locus field. BT's are pipe tables with a 7-value controlled status vocabulary (core_book_thesis 42, local_support 36, core_chapter_thesis 11, methodological 5, core_section_thesis 4, local_argument 3, core_unit_thesis 2); BCAP's are ### headings or Field/Value tables with free-prose Status but an 'Aristotelian texts' locus field BT lacks. BT additionally carries 84 explicit `Linked to: BT-D1-U2-P2` back-references from tension items to specific claims — claim-to-claim connective tissue that already exists. Plus 488 (BT 299 + BCAP 189) typed per-unit edges in fenced JSON, 367 appendix lemmas with unit + page scoping, and ~1,718 quoted strings. NONE of it reaches runtime. This materially lowers the cost of the claim-level programme: it is a parse-and-normalise job for these two entries, not an authoring job. Clause level is genuinely absent everywhere.

3. Compiler-side corruption is systemic, not entry-specific. scripts/compile-corpus-index.py `_parse_header_section` has an unreachable `break` (the `elif current_key and stripped:` branch precedes `elif stripped.startswith("###")`), so in EVERY header-format ontology the last node of each tier absorbs the following section header and the file's last node absorbs everything to EOF. In BT this produces `Temporalität.units` with 586 elements and a 247-char centralityTier, plus corrupted tiers on Resoluteness and Destruktion. Every other header-format entry in TEXT_DIRS (VLE, Boredom Experiment, Boredom Secondary, VR Pedagogy, Social Presence, Presence Theory, Rhetoric of Interactivity, FCM, Rickert, Uexkull, both Burkes, Heidegger and Rhetoric, Calleja, Gross, Wendt) is exposed to the same bug — worth checking corpus-wide.

PRIOR-CLAIM VERDICTS

- "~310 unit records, 691 unit analyses, ~9,762 distinct edges on disk; ZERO reach runtime." PARTIAL. Counts for this batch: 30 unit records (BT 17 + BCAP 13, excluding the 2 manifest.json), 30 unit analyses, 865 distinct edges on disk (BT 284 CSV + 299 per-unit; BCAP 93 CSV + 189 per-unit). "ZERO reach runtime" is REFUTED at the node/tension layer — 74 ontologyNodes and 16 tensionEdges from this batch ARE in compiled-index.json. It is CONFIRMED at the edge layer: 0 of 865 edges reach runtime, as do 0 of 258 claims, 0 of 367 appendix lemmas, 0 of 79 matrix rows, 0 of 203 .mmd arrows.

- "The compiler reads only 4 filename patterns … plus tension-edges.json." The prior audit only checked *.json files; embedded JSON — which is where ALL 488 per-unit edges in this batch live — was never parse-checked.

Neither entry was on the prior list, which suggests the true number of divergent entries is materially higher than four.

BATCH-BRIEF ASSERTIONS TESTED
- "BT: 53 files, 17 units (the 18th .json IS manifest.json)" — CONFIRMED. 53 files; bt-structured contains 18 .json = 17 units + manifest.json; manifest total_units == 17.
- "BCAP: 42 files, 13 units" — CONFIRMED. 42 files; bcap-structured contains 14 .json = 13 units + manifest.json; manifest total_units == 13, total_sections == 28 == sum of section_count.
- "Both are structured/analysis-pair layout" — CONFIRMED.
- "Destruktion gets merged across BT and Heidegger and Rhetoric by deduplicate_ontology_nodes keying on lowercased name with no text component" — CONFIRMED (compiled node Destruktion text == "Heidegger - Being and Time; Heidegger and Rhetoric", and its centralityTier arrives corrupted as 'important ### peripheral nodes (10)').
- "Check what OTHER node names collide across these entries" — BT↔BCAP have ZERO mutual collisions (BT names are English/German, BCAP names are Greek script). BT collides outward on 5: Dasein (with Boredom Secondary + FCM), das Man (Boredom Secondary), Truth (Aristotle Complete Works + Metaphysics), Resoluteness (Heidegger and Rhetoric), Destruktion (Heidegger and Rhetoric). BCAP collides outward on 17 — ψυχή, φαντασία, νοῦς, ἐντελέχεια, δύναμις, ἐνέργεια, κίνησις, οὐσία, λόγος, μεσότης, προαίρεσις, ἀρχή, πάθος/πάθη, ἕξις, φρόνησις, ἀρετή, εὐδαιμονία — all with Aristotle works. The collisions are not merely cosmetic: dedup silently overwrote centrality on 4 BT + 9 BCAP nodes and definitions on 1 BT + 15 BCAP nodes, in several cases inverting core and important.

WHAT SURPRISED ME
(a) The corruption is in the RUNTIME artifact, not the source. Both book-level-ontology.md files are clean, well-formed, human-quality documents; compiled-index.json is where the 586-element units array and the garbage tier strings appear. Auditing the source files alone would have found none of it.
(b) The 'unit records' in both entries carry ZERO analysis — they are pure segmentation scaffolds ("Full text not stored due to content constraints"). Every claim, edge, concept and quotation lives in the .md twin. Any headline count of "N unit records" in this corpus overstates the structured content by roughly 100%.
(c) BT's Section 5a is 17 identical copies of a stub that disables the BT↔BCAP bridge "until BCAP ontology exists" — written the day AFTER the BCAP ontology was completed, and while a BCAP-side bridge graph with 20 populated edges already sat on disk.

entries.granularity_gap: The finest STRUCTURED unit is the sub-item inside a unit JSON, not the unit itself — and this is the single most important correction to make about this entry. It encodes 2,924 sub-items across 55 units (463 readings, 425 constructs, 582 concepts, 718 interlocutors, 387 sections, 211 tensions, 138 measures), of which 2,012 of the 2,258 dict-shaped ones carry a page locus. The `readings` array IS claim-level already: each item is a single proposition with a page anchor, an argumentative stance, and a provenance tag distinguishing the source's own claim (FE) from a close paraphrase (FAITHFUL-<author>) from the project's own interpretive extension (P/anticipatory-application). Example from bor-sec-13: {"claim": "Beings' 'telling refusal' in profound boredom is itself 'a telling, i.e. a making manifest' — it announces the very possibilities it withholds…", "type": "READING/CLAIM", "stance": "restates-FCM (fcm-06)", "locus": "p.114-116", "tag": "FAITHFUL-Slaby"}. That is one level below the article and roughly at the target. So the distance to claim-level is NOT authorship — it is schema and addressing: (1) the readings array has 9 incompatible sub-schemas (claim/text/summary; locus/loci/page); (2) reading ids are unqualified local counters that collide across 6 units; (3) `stance` has 162 uncontrolled values with 195 nulls; (4) nothing reaches runtime — the compiler reads no JSON except tension-edges.json, which this entry does not have. A normalization pass over 55 files (unify to {id: 'bor-sec-NN-Rmm', claim, locus, stance∈enum, tag∈enum}) would deliver ~460 addressable claims at a fraction of the cost of re-reading the sources. Clause-level is genuinely absent: no sub-item is smaller than a proposition, and no quoted span carries a character offset or bbox. But the raw material for it is sitting in the prose layer — 1,725 quoted spans of ≥40 characters across the 55 .md analyses (1,026,780 bytes), roughly 31 per unit, the great majority of which sit within 200 characters of a page locus. Those are extractable quotation records today; what they lack is a verbatim-verification link back to the PDF text, which is exactly what the WRAITH verbatim/bbox work exists to supply. Where the entry is structurally incapable of the target: the EDGE layer. 1,918 rows keyed on (source, relation, target) with locus as a free-text note cannot express a claim-to-claim relation, only unit-to-string. And global-edges.csv's dedup key deletes locus outright — 21 rows already lost. Any redesign must move edges from unit-level to claim-level endpoints, or the finest relational data will keep being collapsed by its own synthesis step.
strengths: Provenance tagging is the best thing in this corpus and must survive verbatim. Every claim, edge and bridge carries FE (the source's own published claim) / FAITHFUL-<author> (close paraphrase of a specific passage) / P/anticipatory-application (the project's own interpretive link, never the source's). 67 FE tags plus ~200 FAITHFUL-<author> tags across the unit JSONs, and bridge-sources/anchor-pointers.md:157-161 states the rule explicitly. This is the discipline that makes claim-level indexing safe to build on.

Refusal to fabricate, recorded as data. manifest.json:32 documents that the bor-sec-18 deep-read agent refused to build a unit under a false attribution when the on-disk 'Standish (2015)' PDF turned out to be a mislabeled duplicate of Mertel (2020), verified three ways (pdfinfo Title, Subject 'J Philosophy of Edu 2020.54:467-486', matching CreationDate, and a full-text diff). manifest.json:47-60 similarly refuses to fabricate bridges-to-fcm edges for bor-sec-15/17/19 when the sources genuinely do not engage FCM, and documents the plan's own internal contradiction rather than silently picking a side. Negative findings are first-class data here.

Three bibliographic corrections made AGAINST the plan and against the filenames, each with reproducible evidence: bor-sec-44 authorship (Nacke & Lindley, not 'Lindley & Nacke' and not 'Nacke & Craig' — evidenced by pdftotext -layout column order, PDF Author metadata, and the authors' own self-citations at refs [22]/[23]), bor-sec-38 year (2015 not 2019, from the PLoS ONE citation line 10(6):e0130608), bor-sec-18 attribution (Mansikka 2008 not Standish 2015). manifest.json:35-45 even records that an EARLIER check of bor-sec-44 was itself wrong and why (a non-layout pdftotext dump interleaved the two-column byline).

Haystack extraction handled honestly. bor-sec-40 and bor-sec-41 are single papers extracted from 727pp and 781pp proceedings volumes, with the containers md5-matched, excluded as non-units, and the page ranges recorded (manifest.json:121-122: pdfPageRange 55-64 and 564-568, plus bookPageRange for the latter).

Perfect structural conformance where it matters: 55/55 unit folders exist, 165/165 expected per-unit files present, 0 JSON parse failures across 62 files, 0 missing units, 0 dangling bor-sec-* references in ANY synthesis file (debate-map, citation-network, concordance, terminology appendix, literature network, all 5 .mmd), 0 duplicate node names inside cluster-ontology.json, node headers numbered 1..68 monotonically, all 55 unit .md files carrying exactly 7 second-level headings, and the entry fully committed to git with no working-tree diff.

cluster-ontology.json is genuinely faithful to cluster-ontology.md — generated with the compiler's OWN parse_header_ontology so they cannot drift. Verified: identical 68 node names, identical byType and byCentrality distributions. This is the right pattern and no other entry I know of does it. (The drift is entirely downstream, in the compiler's cross-text merge, not in the entry.)

The synthesis prose is real analysis, not summary. cluster-ontology.md §2 states a substantive structural finding — that the phenomenological and empirical strands independently arrive at the same 'measurement wall' from opposite directions (Heidegger's awakening-vs-ascertaining at FCM §16 p.59; Kim et al.'s null self-report/physiology correlation at bor-sec-28 N=13; Charoenpit & Ohkura's own correlation tables contradicting their stated rule at bor-sec-35; Perone et al.'s unsupported H1 at bor-sec-30 N=54) — and flags it as the cluster's strongest joint claim. graph-construct-measure-density.mmd draws the payoff: the three FCM-form constructs are reachable by self-report and nothing else. That is an authored finding, not a rollup, and it is the kind of thing a claim-level index should be able to reproduce mechanically.

The concordance reports a GAP rather than manufacturing a mapping, and names its own category error: boredom-construct-measure-concordance.json gridStats records the empty 'predictive-processing model' column as 'A category error inherited from the plan's own measure axis, not a gap in the literature… Recommendation: move this out of the measure axis in any successor grid,' and records that a first pass wrongly attributed it to bor-sec-39 on a substring match, corrected by hand.

No encoding damage. Targeted scan for pdfium ligature loss (benefcial/signifcant/specifc/identifed/classifed/defnition/fxation/confdence/…) across all 189 files returned 0 hits — the pdftotext-based extraction path avoided the known corpus-wide hazard.
entries.verdict: Sound in substance, structurally under-served by the pipeline it feeds, and mis-nominated as a gold standard for the wrong reason. As an act of scholarship this entry is the best thing in corpus/index/: its manifest is the only one I tested where every declared count and every declared source path survives contact with the filesystem (55/55 units, 55/55 sourceFiles resolvable, 50/50 PDFs, 7/7 strand counts, 165/165 expected files, 0 JSON parse failures, 0 dangling unit references anywhere), its provenance tagging (FE / FAITHFUL-<author> / P/anticipatory-application) is the discipline the whole programme should standardize on, and it records three bibliographic corrections against its own plan plus a documented refusal to fabricate a unit — negative findings treated as first-class data. Judged against its own cluster template it is close to a pass, with real but repairable defects: five self-declared counts in cluster-ontology.md §8 are wrong (72 vs 70 citation edges, 24 TERM vs 25, 12 DEBATE-AXIS vs 8, METHOD omitted, 274 vs 260 matrix cells); phase0-overview.md still says 46 units and 2 Strand-G units; three files insist the Boredom Experiment entry 'does not exist' when it has for two weeks; and the cluster-ontology.json compilerNote claims a compiler patch is still required when the fallback shipped. Judged against the claim/clause-level target the verdict is sharper and more useful: this entry ALREADY contains ~463 claim-level readings and ~2,012 page-anchored sub-items, plus ~1,725 quoted spans in prose — it is not two granularity levels short of the goal, it is one schema normalization and one addressing scheme short. What blocks it is not authorship but plumbing: 9 incompatible readings sub-schemas, three interchangeable locus keys, reading ids (C1..C19) that collide across six units, a 162-value uncontrolled stance vocabulary, 46 free-text debate-axis targets that cannot join to DA-01..DA-11, and a compiler that reads 37,664 bytes of one markdown section and ignores the other 3.39 MB — so ~1.1% of authored content reaches runtime and 1,918 edges plus 211 tensions plus 11 debate axes reach nothing. Two findings should change the redesign's priorities. First, global-edges.csv is not a duplicate serialization but a LOSSY projection: it is exactly the distinct (source, relation, target) triples, so it has already destroyed the locus and note of 21 rows, 12 of them bridges-to-fcm — the dedup key deletes precisely the passage-level evidence the goal requires. This makes Boredom Secondary a fifth entry where the two edge layers disagree, but the only one that documents the rule (cluster-ontology.md:133), which is why the discrepancy is defensible here and silent elsewhere. Second, the compiler's name-keyed merge (scripts/compile-corpus-index.py:1311-1348) silently overwrites this cluster's authored definitions of Dasein, das Man, Pathos, Kairos and Enthymeme with longer definitions from other entries — so the cluster's distinctive readings of shared concepts are the only part of its ontology that gets discarded, while the node still LOOKS attributed to it. Verdict: do not rebuild. Normalize and re-address. The reading data, the provenance tags, the corrections ledger, the concordance's honest gap-reporting and the manifest's exclusion accounting must all survive verbatim; what must be replaced is the edge model (unit-to-string → claim-to-claim), the synthesis dedup (drop it, or key on all five columns), and the registration path (read the JSON, not one markdown section).

12. "Per-source *-edges.csv and _synthesis/global-edges.csv are the SAME data serialized twice, but four entries disagree… Nothing records which is stale." — REFUTED as stated, for this entry, and the correction generalizes. They are NOT the same data serialized twice. Here global-edges.csv is provably the set of distinct (source, relation, target) triples: distinct triples per-unit = 1,897 = global row count exactly; distinct 5-tuples per-unit = 1,918; per-unit 5-tuples missing from global = 21; global rows missing from per-unit = 0; exact duplicate 5-tuples within the per-unit layer = 0. So the synthesis layer is a LOSSY PROJECTION that deletes locus and note — the finest evidence in the entry — for every row that shares a triple with another. This makes Boredom Secondary a FIFTH disagreeing entry (1,918 vs 1,897) that the prior audit missed, and it is the only one that documents the rule (cluster-ontology.md:133: "1,897 deduplicated edges in global-edges.csv (raw 1,918 before dedup)"). Recommendation for the other four: test whether their deltas are also (s,r,t) collapses before assuming staleness. If FCM's 428-vs-452 and Phantasia's 708-vs-706 have the same signature, the corpus does not have a staleness problem, it has a schema problem — and the fix is to stop deduping, or to make locus part of the key.

CROSS-CUTTING FINDING NOT IN ANY PRIOR CLAIM, and the one I would act on first: the compiler's cross-text node merge (scripts/compile-corpus-index.py:1311-1348) keys on `node["name"].lower()` and keeps only the LONGEST definition while unioning `units` and concatenating `text` with "; ". The same merge also pollutes units arrays with junk tokens harvested from other entries' ontologies ('all', '17', 'units', 'Ch1', 'Intro', 'Conclusion', 'D1-U4', 'RHET-01-04-06'), which then appear on nodes this cluster authored. Any redesign that keeps a shared canonical-term space needs per-text definition slots, not a longest-wins merge.

SECOND CROSS-CUTTING FINDING: parse_header_ontology truncates node names at a parenthesis and files the parenthetical into the `greek` slot. `#### 32. Motivation model (gaze-based)` (cluster-ontology.md:367) becomes name="Motivation model", greek="gaze-based", and BOTH land in compiled-index.json canonicalTerms. Worth sweeping every header-format entry for both patterns.

That is one level below chapter, not two: a page is not a claim and certainly not a clause. HOWEVER — claim-level material is already present in quantity, just unstructured or unreachable. (1) 71 unit-level `positions` across the 13 deep JSONs are already true claim records (e.g. ig-10-deep.json positions[0] = {id:'P01', label:'Incorporation displaces immersion+presence as primary theoretical frame', anchor:'pp.167-169 + 172', summary:'…'}) — they need only a stable ID scheme and a canonical slot. (2) 45 unit tensions + 12 volume tensions are claim-vs-claim oppositions with page anchors. (3) 18 canonical POSITIONs in book-level-ontology.json carry `claim` + `supporting_units` and are the closest thing to a claim ontology in the whole corpus — and they reach nothing. (4) 995 line-range anchors are already sub-page, i.e. clause-adjacent — this is the single largest latent asset in the entry, and it is worthless only because /tmp/calleja-fulltext.txt was deleted; regenerating that file with a recorded, deterministic extraction command would resurrect ~1,000 clause-level pointers in one step. (5) 47,443 words of deep prose analysis (13 *-deep.md) contain hundreds of further claim-level assertions with inline page cites, entirely unstructured. What is structurally MISSING and cannot be recovered: verbatim clause text. The entry deliberately suppresses it — ig-10-deep.json:434-441 `content_filter_audit` records that every ≥25-word block was paraphrased, and ig-00-deep.json:222 / ig-02-deep.json:330 assert 'no ≥25-word verbatim from Calleja'. A clause-level index needs the clause. So: claim-level is ~70% of the way there and cheap (promote positions/tensions, give them IDs, register them); clause-level requires re-extracting from the PDF under a policy change, and the line-anchor scaffolding to hang it on must be rebuilt first.
strengths: Falsification is recorded, not hidden. manifest.json `cite_check.gibson` states 'CRITICAL FINDING — GIBSON ABSENT, AFFORDANCE GENERIC … The Gibson-as-implicit-Uexküll-bridge hypothesis (plan v3 §5 Phase 0) is FALSIFIED', with the 11 generic 'affordance' hits counted and the downstream implication spelled out. Negative findings of this quality are rare and must survive any redesign.

Provenance typing on every edge. The 736-row global-edges.csv carries a `provenance` column distinguishing text-anchored / calleja-exegetical / anticipatory-projection (dissertation) / mediated-exegetical, and the manifest fixes the default per layer. This is the cleanest exegesis-vs-augmentation separation I saw and is exactly what a claim-level index needs to avoid attributing the dissertation's claims to Calleja.

Verified quotation fidelity where quotations survive. The canonical incorporation definition stored at ig-10-deep.json concepts[0] matches Calleja p.169 word-for-word apart from two dropped connectives; the four Lakoff+Johnson cite locations in `lakoff_johnson_damasio_dennett_role` each carry page + line + surrounding context.

The 10,078-word ig-pim-operationalization-manual.md plus its JSON twin (sections A-E: six dimension entries, incorporation rubric, WoW worked example, analytic question battery, three-layer augmentation) is the single most reusable artifact here — an operational instrument, not a summary.

contested-nodes.md documents 10 nodes with an explicit five-way taxonomy of contest types (internal contradiction / cross-unit incompatibility / cite-base mismatch / structural defect / acknowledged under-development), each with canonical ID, page anchors and dissertation implications. entries.verdict: Salvageable, and worth salvaging — but the current serialization must be rebuilt. Judged against its own cluster template the entry is one of the strongest in the corpus: 13 chapters exhaustively covered, a real Phase-0 cite-check that falsified its own plan's central bridge hypothesis, per-edge provenance typing, an operational manual, and a resolution report that confesses its own data loss. Judged against the runtime it is near-total waste: 44 ontology nodes reach compiled-index.json and nothing else does — not the 736 edges, not the 18 canonical positions, not the 12 tensions (silently zeroed by a schema mismatch), not the 180 mermaid arrows, not 47,443 words of analysis. Judged against the claim/clause-level target it is structurally capable at claim level and structurally INCAPABLE at clause level: the 71 unit positions and 18 canonical positions are already claim records needing only IDs and a slot, and the 995 line-range anchors are already clause-adjacent — but the entry deliberately deleted the clause text (content_filter: no ≥25-word verbatim) and deleted the line-numbered fulltext those anchors point into. Rebuild priorities, in order: (1) fix the one-character JSON break at ig-10-incorporation.json:155; (2) regenerate /tmp/calleja-fulltext.txt under a recorded deterministic command and re-validate the 995 anchors; (3) impose one edge-CSV schema and one per-unit ID scheme, which alone fixes the 58% endpoint-resolution failure; (4) give POSITIONs a canonical slot the compiler reads; (5) normalise tension-edges.json to node_a/node_b. Do not preserve: the three self-certifying quality_gate_status blocks, global-edges-pre-canonical.csv (a false backup), and the tier_distribution summary blocks — all of them report numbers that contradict the data in the same file.

entries.verdict: Sound in its analysis, broken in its plumbing — salvage the content, discard the serialization. The odd ratio the brief flags (6 units, 36 nodes, '744 edge rows') resolves cleanly: the units are whole chapters of 18-34 book pages each, every one yielding 22-43 concepts, 8-11 positions, 6-9 tensions and 30-44 interlocutors, so ~62 edges per unit is proportionate; and 744 is not a real quantity — it is 373 per-unit rows plus 371 synthesis rows, the same edges serialized twice, with the two layers disagreeing by 2 because the synthesis merge collapsed distinct page-level loci (merleau-ponty-phenomenology-84 + -172n1 -> merleau-ponty-phenomenology-of-perception). This entry has the best evidence hygiene in the batch — page anchors throughout, all JSON parsing, all derived counts correct, three claims independently re-verified against the PDF, and the only render validation in the corpus. It also has the worst identity hygiene: four incompatible ID namespaces for one concept set (US-C-###, C-US-##, C0##, ad-hoc surname tokens), two of six units with no record IDs at all, five header dialects across six edge files, and a concept-matrix that shares zero IDs and three names with the ontology it claims to accompany. Against the claim/clause target it is the most promising entry I examined: 55 unit positions + 18 canonical positions already have claimant/claim/support/contested_by, and 176 concordance loci already sit at phrase level with dual page anchors. It needs (1) tension-edges.json normalised from pole_A/pole_B to node_a/node_b, (2) one ID namespace, retro-applied, with the concept-matrix reconciled to the ontology or deleted, (3) positions given a slot the compiler reads, (4) the synthesis edge layer either deleted in favour of the per-unit layer or made lossless with a recorded join key, (5) the two ragged rows in us-05-epilogue-edges.csv quoted properly, (6) the content-filter relaxed enough to store the clause alongside the gloss. Do not rebuild the analysis — it is correct where I tested it.

All 7 declared source paths resolve today. However 3 of 7 sha256 values no longer match the bytes on disk (DISS-00-INTRO, DISS-04-EMOTION, DISS-05-A4) and nothing flags this. Of 161 distinct corpus/ or tmp/ file paths grepped out of the entry, 141 resolve and 20 do not — of which ~6 are genuine dangling references and the rest are grep artifacts from prose (e.g. 'corpus/index AND from the .md'). Schema is not uniform inside one manifest: DISS-02-A1A2 omits bytes_prior/words_prior/lines_prior that DISS-00 and DISS-01 carry, and DISS-DIAG-V7 uses `"lines_approx": "see file"` instead of an integer.

entries.granularity_gap: This entry is the exception in the whole corpus index: it ALREADY encodes claim-level granularity, and it does so structurally, not incidentally. 982 distinct claim records (306 for §1.4 alone) across 56,713 words of source prose = one record per ~58 words, which is roughly sentence granularity. 100% carry a line anchor (`ln` string or `location` {line_start,line_end}); 76% participate in an explicit supports/supported_by graph; every record carries a typed support tier from an 8-level legend (T1 textually-confirmed 277, T2 78, T3 interpretive-but-flagged 477, T4 41, T5 71, T6 12, T7 overreach 22, T8 secondary-needed 4); 38% record the primary citations actually present in the text; 11% record `implicit_citations_needed` with a candidate locus, a tier, and a rationale; and nearly all carry a `remediation` object naming an action plus corpus-index / ChromaDB / Perplexity candidates and an effort estimate. Below claim level, the entry also holds genuinely CLAUSE-level material: 841 typed edges whose `target` column is 53% claim-IDs and 47% free-text loci (ARISTOTLE-LOCUS:'DA III.7 431a8-12', HEIDEGGER-LOCUS:'SZ §29 H.137', SECONDARY-LOCUS:'Burke Grammar pp. 280-28', SECTION:DISS-02-A1A2); 235 cached verbatim quotations each with author/year/page, an `insertion_anchor` naming the exact phrase in the target text, a use designation (in-text/footnote/epigraph) and a rationale; and 156 citation-fill markdown files that pair a verbatim with the exact current sentence it is to attach to, plus a ready-to-paste MLA/LaTeX form. Spot-verified: the Christensen 2016 verbatim in cache-Q-CHR-05.md reproduces corpus/download/_extra_Aristotle_20on_20Anger_20Justice_20and_20Punishment.pdf exactly. So the cost of the claim/clause-level programme for this entry is NOT extraction — it is (a) schema unification across six dialects, (b) promoting the 156 citation-fill .md files and the free-text LOCUS strings into resolvable IDs, and (c) re-anchoring against the 3 drifted sources. The one structural limit: all of it is about the user's OWN prose, not about a source text. To serve the stated goal for SOURCES, this schema would have to be re-pointed at corpus documents — but it is a working, proven, claim-level schema and the only one in the index.
strengths: The 982-record claim layer is the single most valuable structured asset in the corpus index and must survive any redesign intact: line-anchored, typed by claim_type and logical_role, tiered T1-T8 by evidential support, wired into a supports/supported_by DAG (76% participation), and carrying a machine-readable remediation object with routing candidates and effort estimates.

Manifest provenance is exemplary: sha256 + bytes + lines + words for every input, and run 2 additionally stores sha256_prior_run and per-field deltas. This is what let me prove 3-of-7 source drift in one command — no other entry in the batch supports that.

The 156 citation-fill artifacts are a genuine clause-level bridge: verbatim + full source + page + the exact current sentence in the target text + anchor-match classification + routing tier + ready-to-paste MLA/LaTeX form. Spot-verified accurate against the source PDF.
The 235-entry parsed citation cache with insertion_anchor + use designation + rationale is a reusable quotation-placement index, and its id_prefix_to_source map documents 22 source abbreviations.

concept-matrix.csv is internally consistent: 81 concepts x 6 sections, and the `sections_used` integer matches the count of marked cells on all 81 rows with zero mismatches; centrality is a closed 3-value vocabulary (core 28 / important 21 / supporting 32).
Run 2 unified the citation-gap-table.json schema across all six sections (1 signature vs run 1's 6) — evidence the pipeline was already converging on a single dialect.

The .md inheritance protocol is explicit and honest where it exists: run 2's phase2-claims.md files carry `<!-- Inherited from 2026-05-13T1439 (claim-IDs preserved per plan §14 diff-protocol) -->`. The fix for the .json layer is to apply the same marker.

The entry documents its own methodological failures rather than hiding them — marathon_workflow_rules_logged Rule 5 in run 2's manifest states 'Pipeline analysis can be wrong' and records a case where the pipeline's citation correction was verified WRONG against MIT Classics Archive. That epistemic honesty is rare and worth preserving.
Every one of the 69 JSON and 2 JSONL files parses cleanly.
entries.verdict: SALVAGEABLE AND STRATEGICALLY IMPORTANT — but its classification as a 'pipeline run-history store, not a source-text entry' is only half right, and the half that is wrong is the half that matters. It is correctly not a source-text entry: it indexes the user's own dissertation prose, not a corpus document, and it belongs in TEXT_DIRS in no form the current compiler understands (it has no ontology file, no cluster-ontology, no tension-edges.json, no .mmd). But calling it 'run history' undersells it: this is the only entry in the corpus index that has actually built the thing the user says he wants. 982 line-anchored, tier-typed, graph-wired claim records with remediation routing is claim-level indexing, working, at 1 record per 58 words. The prior audit's 'ZERO reaches runtime' is also only half right for this entry — zero reaches compiled-index.json, but 273 markdown files (571 chunks) are recorded as successfully ingested into ChromaDB with all hashes still matching, so the prose narration IS retrievable while the structured findings are not. That is the exact inversion of what should be true. The defects are real and numerous — six incompatible claim schemas in one run, run 2's claim JSONs being unmarked byte-copies of run 1 carrying stale run_ids and a superseded input hash, a gap-master whose declared per-section counts contradict its own array in two sections, a severity histogram that sums to 210 against a stated 207, a citation cache that advertises 244/235/213 entries in three places, one pdfium ligature corruption and one silent verbatim alteration in quotations destined for the body text, and two 'authoritative' pointer files that disagree with each other and with every JSON they summarise on every headline number. None of that is a reason to rebuild. All of it is a schema-unification and provenance-marking job over an extraction that has already been paid for. The right move is: (1) freeze run 1 as the extraction of record and delete or explicitly mark run 2's duplicated JSON/CSV layer, (2) normalise the six claim dialects to the compact DISS-00/02/04 form, (3) promote the free-text ARISTOTLE-LOCUS/HEIDEGGER-LOCUS edge targets and the 156 citation-fill files into resolvable IDs against the Aristotle/BCAP/BT entries, (4) re-anchor the three drifted sources, and (5) treat this schema as the TEMPLATE for the claim-level programme across source-text entries rather than as an oddity to be archived.

provenance.notes: There is NO manifest and therefore no machine-readable source declaration of any kind; all provenance is prose in document headers. That places this entry squarely in the 'no machine-readable source path' class. Of 35 backtick-quoted file paths grepped from the markdown, 23 resolve (many only after searching the whole repo, since the references are bare filenames with no directory) and 12 do not; 2 of the 12 are genuinely unrecoverable. Offsetting this: the cross-entry unit references DO resolve. I verified all 7 (ig-04, ig-07, ig-10, rm-01, rm-04, rm-05, rm-07) against corpus/index/In-Game (Calleja 2011)/ and corpus/index/A Rhetoric of Motives (Burke 1950)/ — every one exists as a real unit file, modulo case. And I verified v9's quotation practice directly: 4 of 5 sampled quotations appear verbatim in the declared verification file tmp/Dissertation/verbatim_passages.md, and the Rickert p.246 quotation reproduces corpus/rhetorical_ontology/Rickert, Thomas - Ambient Rhetoric...pdf exactly with a properly-marked elision. entries.granularity_gap: This entry sits at the OPPOSITE end from the batch's other member: its finest unit of analysis is the whole method-document, and there is no unit layer at all — no per-section records, no claim records, no edges, no ontology. Its structured content is exactly 11 crosswalk bindings in validated-crosswalk.json (4 core bijective + 4 many-to-many cluster + 3 secondary ties, 0 rejected), each with pentad term, PIM dimension, strength, status, both_directions flag, and a per-direction textual warrant. That is 11 records for 82,134 words — roughly 1 structured record per 7,500 words, three to four orders of magnitude coarser than the claim/clause target. BUT the entry is dense with material that is ALREADY claim-level and merely unstructured. Quantifying what a extraction pass would find: 68 quoted strings of 25+ characters in CANONICAL-METHODOLOGY-v9.md alone, 24 distinct Bekker loci in that one file, and a fully-enumerated diagnostic vocabulary that is effectively a claim schema in disguise — R1 assimilation, R2 embodiment, R3 simultaneity, R4 cornerstone, R5 blending, R6 temporal-apex, R7 intrusion-integration appear 68/35/40/26/34/42/78 times respectively across the markdown (323 coded assertions), each attached in the VALIDATION files to specific timestamps in one game episode. THE-MATRIX.md is literally a claim-extraction form: chain locus x what-happens x three-factor-motion x designed-channel x doxa/hexis/affect, with an R1-R7 criterion table underneath. So the raw material for a claim-level encoding of THIS method exists and is well-disciplined; what is missing is (a) any ID scheme for the propositions, (b) any file that holds a filled-in MATRIX (the worksheet in the index is BLANK — every data cell is empty), and (c) any edge table linking the 11 crosswalk bindings, the 7 R-criteria, the A0-A4 chain nodes, and the sibling entries' units. Critically, this entry is not a source-text index at all — it is the INSTRUMENT that would be applied to source texts. Judged by (a) its own standard, it is a well-versioned, empirically-checked, cross-validated methodology with an honest changelog and mostly-verified quotations. Judged by (b) the claim/clause-level target, it is structurally incapable in its current form: there is nothing to encode claims ABOUT, because the entry indexes no document. Its correct role in the redesign is as the SCHEMA SOURCE — the R1-R7 criteria, the A0-A4 chain loci, the 6x6 Burke×Calleja grid and the four-cause/seven-cause frame are exactly the controlled vocabulary a claim-level game-analysis encoding would need — not as an entry to be given unit records of its own.
strengths: The version chain is genuinely disciplined and self-documenting: every canonical file opens with a Date/Status/base-Status header, an explicit statement of what changed and what did not, and a named audit document. v9:14 even explains why there is no v7 ('framed as v7 in the audit, realized as v8 per direction'). Nothing is silently overwritten.

validated-crosswalk.json is real bidirectional validation, not a mapping guess: meta.provenance_note states plainly 'All pentad<->PIM bindings are anticipatory-projection (neither Burke nor Calleja makes the cross-claim). Validation upgrades epistemic status from one-directional guess to bidirectionally-warranted; it does not make them author claims.' Every binding carries a burke_warrant AND a calleja_warrant. rejected_bindings is an explicit empty array rather than an omission.

All 7 cross-entry unit references (IG-04, IG-07, IG-10, RM-01, RM-04, RM-05, RM-07) resolve to real unit files in the In-Game and Rhetoric of Motives entries. This is the only true cross-entry bridge layer I found in the batch and it is accurate.

The quotation practice is better than the entry's file-path practice: 4 of 5 sampled v9 quotations verify verbatim against the declared tmp/Dissertation/verbatim_passages.md, and the Rickert p.246 quotation reproduces the corpus PDF exactly with a correctly-marked elision. Where verification failed, the text carries an explicit `****** page unverified` marker per the project's own placeholder convention rather than asserting.

Seven successive validation runs against the same episode (the Valentine saloon brawl) constitute a real regression suite for a methodology — including an independent v6-blind re-derivation reported as '62 convergences across ten dimensions, zero surviving overreach'. Very few methodology documents anywhere carry this.

The R1-R7 incorporation criteria and the A0-A4 chain loci form a tight, closed, repeatedly-used controlled vocabulary (323 coded occurrences across the markdown) — ready-made as the term set for a structured game-analysis schema.

v9's changelog is honest about its own debts: it records rather than conceals that ontological-wiring-A0-A4.md and THE-MATRIX.md still carry stale framing, and it flags rather than asserts citations it believed unverifiable.
The one JSON file parses cleanly.
entries.verdict: MISCLASSIFIED AND MUST BE REBUILT AS SOMETHING ELSE — but almost none of its content should be discarded. Calling this an 'analysis artifact' is closer than calling it a source-text entry, yet both labels miss what it is: it is a METHODOLOGICAL INSTRUMENT plus its regression suite, living in a directory whose conventions assume indexed source documents. It has no units, no unit analyses, no edges, no ontology, no manifest, and no .mmd, and it is unregistered in TEXT_DIRS, so its compiled-index contribution is exactly zero. What it does have is 61 chunks in ChromaDB — and here the batch brief is wrong twice over: it is NOT the only index content live in ChromaDB (scripts/ingest/manifest.jsonl records 524 successful corpus/index rows across 13 entries, including 273 files and 571 chunks from the Dissertation entry in this same batch), and its ingested slice is not '25 chunks from 6 PDFs' but 61 chunks from 8 documents, of which 25 come from 4 PDFs. The genuinely damning finding is which 8: the ingested set contains the superseded v1 methodology and a PDF built from it (build_pdf.py:25-28), while all seven canonical versions including v9 are unreachable — so the only retrievable form of a method that two other corpus entries declare as their methodology_target is a month-old, seven-revisions-stale document, and the RDR2 entry's pointer to v9 is itself broken by an ASCII-versus-U+00D7 mismatch. Beneath that sit two evidence problems the entry itself documents: the bar-fight transcript that grounds all seven validation runs was destroyed by a reboot and validations v4 onward are re-readings of v3's prose, and v9 marks three load-bearing quotations unverifiable on the false premise that the Burke and Rickert PDFs are absent from the corpus when both are present and I verified the Rickert line against one of them in a single command. The redesign should: promote v9 (and only v9) to the ingested canonical with the older versions moved to a versions/ subtree or dropped to git history, write a manifest declaring canonical version and inputs, fix the RDR2 inbound path, case-fold the cross-entry IDs so validated-crosswalk.json becomes a real edge table, re-derive or archive the bar-fight transcript, clear the three false-negative citation flags, and — most importantly — lift the R1-R7 criteria, the A0-A4 loci and the 6x6 grid out of prose into the shared controlled vocabulary, so this entry stops being a document to index and becomes the schema that lets game-analysis entries be indexed at claim level.

result.batch_notes:
CROSS-ENTRY OBSERVATION. The two entries in this batch are near-perfect inverses and together they falsify the framing that the index is uniformly coarse and uniformly dead. "Dissertation" has the finest granularity in the entire corpus index (982 line-anchored, tier-typed, graph-wired claim records = 1 per ~58 words of source) and the best provenance apparatus (sha256 + bytes + lines + words per input, with prior-run deltas), but zero of it is registered anywhere and 62% of its bytes reach nothing. "Game-Behavior" has essentially no granularity (11 structured bindings for 82,134 words) but is the batch's only true CROSS-ENTRY bridge — 7 unit IDs referencing In-Game and Rhetoric of Motives, all of which resolve. Neither is in TEXT_DIRS. The programme does not need to invent a claim-level schema; one already exists and works, in the entry least likely to be looked at.

VERDICTS ON PRIOR CLAIMS

1. "~310 unit records, 691 unit analyses, ~9,762 distinct edges on disk; ZERO reach runtime." — PARTIAL, and the "ZERO" is materially misleading. CONFIRMED for compiled-index.json: `json.dumps(corpus/index/compiled-index.json).count('Dissertation')` = 0, `.count('DISS-')` = 0, `.count('Game-Behavior')` = 0, `.count('RODA')` = 0. REFUTED as a statement about runtime generally: scripts/ingest/manifest.jsonl records 772 rows under corpus/index/, of which 524 are status 'ok' across 13 entries. Dissertation contributes 273 rows / 571 chunks, ALL status 'ok', and all 273 sha256 still match disk today (0 drifted, 0 missing). Game-Behavior contributes 10 rows / 8 distinct files / 61 chunks, all 'ok'. So markdown DOES reach a vector store; it is precisely the structured layer (all 69 .json, all 14 .csv, both .jsonl in Dissertation; validated-crosswalk.json in GBAM) that reaches nothing. Also note 248 of the 772 corpus/index ingest rows FAILED with the identical error `cannot access local variable 'bbox_chunks' where it is not associated with a value` (e.g. every Aristotle ontology and cross-pipeline-hooks file) — a third reachability failure mode nobody has named. My batch's contribution to the on-disk totals: 45 per-unit JSON records + 55 per-unit md analyses + 841 distinct edge rows (1,682 serialized across two runs; the run-2 CSVs are byte-identical to run-1, so any global edge census that counted 1,682 here double-counted).

2. "The compiler reads only 4 filename patterns … plus tension-edges.json." — CONFIRMED. scripts/compile-corpus-index.py:1181-1275: collect_ontology_nodes() opens only `<analysis_subdir>/book-level-ontology.md`, falls back to `cluster-ontology.md`, and for the Aristotle 'table' format globs `*-ontology.md`; collect_cross_pipeline_hooks() globs `*-cross-pipeline-hooks.md` under the Aristotle dir only (:1238 comment "Only Aristotle has cross-pipeline hook files"); collect_tension_edges() opens `<analysis_subdir>/tension-edges.json`. TEXT_DIRS at :35-133 has exactly 20 keys; neither of my entries is among them. Neither entry contains any file matching any of the five patterns, so registration alone would still yield 0 nodes for both.

3. "42 edge-CSV header dialects, 633 relation values, 31 unenforced ID prefixes." — NOT GLOBALLY TESTED (out of batch scope), but my batch's contribution is measured: exactly 1 edge-CSV header dialect (`source_claim,relation,edge_domain,target,note,location`, identical across all 12 files), 17 relation values, 23 edge_domain values, and 2 ID namespaces in the edge layer (`DISS-nn-Cnnn` for 975 rows across source/target, and an undeclared `CONCEPT:` namespace on 7 rows that resolves to nothing). Worth flagging for the global census: the relation vocabulary is internally inconsistent in casing (`depends_on`, `contrasts_with` alongside `cites-as-support`, `inconsistent-with`) and edge_domain contains case-variant near-duplicates (`Heidegger` 3 / `Heideggerian` 2, `interpretive` 4 / `interpretive-bridge` 7), so a naive distinct-value count over the whole corpus is inflated.

4. "Only ~10 manifests record source PDFs; 9 entries have NO machine-readable source path." — CONFIRMED for Game-Behavior (no manifest.json at all; every source reference is prose in a document header, and 12 of 35 grepped paths do not resolve). REFUTED for Dissertation, which is at the opposite extreme: 2 manifests, 7 inputs each, every one with path + sha256 + bytes + lines + words, and run 2 adding sha256_prior_run/bytes_delta/words_delta. All 7 paths resolve. This is the strongest source-provenance record I saw, which is what made it possible to prove 3-of-7 sources have drifted since indexing.

5. "Only 2 of 27 entries have a quality-gates-report.md; only 1 has machine-readable metrics." — PARTIAL / misleading for Dissertation. There is no file named quality-gates-report.md, so the filename-based count is right. But machine-readable `quality_gates` objects are embedded in at least 6 JSONs (phase2-claims.json for DISS-01 and DISS-05, citation-gap-table.json for DISS-00/01/03/05, citation-gap-master.json). The catch is that they are unreliable: DISS-01's gate declares `"edge_count": "see phase2-edges.csv (target 40-80; produced 56)"` against an actual 101 rows (so a gate that should have FAILED is recorded as passing), and DISS-05's declares "yes (96 vs expected 80-120)" in a file whose own `total_claims` is 98. Gate VALUES are free-text strings mixing booleans and prose, so they cannot be validated mechanically. A filename-based census understates gate coverage and overstates gate quality.

6. "ig-10-incorporation.json is the only unparseable JSON of 494." — CONSISTENT. 0 parse failures across my batch's 70 JSON files (69 Dissertation + 1 GBAM) and 2 JSONL files (19 valid lines each, 0 bad).

7. "4 of 11 tension-edges.json files yield ZERO edges silently." — N/A. Neither entry contains a tension-edges.json. compiled-index.json ships 64 tensionEdges, none attributable to my batch.

8. "67 .mmd files across 15 entries encode 1,544 arrow-edges reachable by nothing." — CONSISTENT. 0 .mmd files in either entry. (GBAM does hold 3 .html diagram files — METHODOLOGY-DIAGRAM.html, DIA-unified-framework-diagram.html, ADA-Advisor-Brief.html — none ingested, none compiled, so the same class of unreachable-diagram problem exists here in a different format that an .mmd-only census would miss.)

9. "144 cross_pipeline_bridges in 22 unit JSONs; runtime has 72 hooks, 100% Aristotle." — CONFIRMED on the runtime side: compiled-index.json has exactly 72 crossPipelineHooks, and compile-corpus-index.py:1238 restricts hook collection to the Aristotle directory by construction. Neither of my entries contributes any.

10. "35 *-deep.json files … no canonical slot." — N/A to my batch (0 *-deep.json), but note GBAM references seven of them by ID (ig-04/07/10-deep, rm-01/04/05/07-deep) from validated-crosswalk.json and CANONICAL-METHODOLOGY-v5.md:266. So the *-deep.json layer has at least one real would-be consumer; it is not merely orphaned.

11. "Per-source and _synthesis edge CSVs are the same data twice; four entries disagree; nothing records which is stale." — N/A in that exact form (Dissertation has no _synthesis edge CSV), but the SAME pathology appears here on a different axis: run-2's six phase2-edges.csv and its concept-matrix.csv are byte-identical to run-1's (cmp -s IDENTICAL on all seven), and nothing records that run 2's copies are inherited. The .md files under run 2 DO carry an explicit `<!-- Inherited from 2026-05-13T1439 -->` marker; the .json and .csv files carry none. So the inheritance-marking convention exists in this codebase and was applied to exactly one of three file classes.

WHAT SURPRISED ME

— The Dissertation entry has already solved the claim-level problem. 982 records, 100% line-anchored, 76% in a supports/supported_by DAG, tiered T1-T8 (T1 277 / T2 78 / T3 477 / T4 41 / T5 71 / T6 12 / T7 22 / T8 4), 38% recording the primary citations actually present in the text, 11% recording implicit-citations-needed with locus + tier + rationale, and nearly all carrying a remediation object with corpus/ChromaDB/Perplexity routing candidates and an effort estimate. Plus 156 citation-fill markdown files that pair a verbatim with the exact current sentence it attaches to and a ready-to-paste MLA/LaTeX form. The claim-level programme's cost for this entry is schema unification, not extraction.

— Quotation fidelity is measurably real, and measurably broken, in the same file. I verified the Christensen 2016 verbatim in cache-Q-CHR-05.md character-for-character against corpus/download/_extra_Aristotle_20on_20Anger_20Justice_20and_20Punishment.pdf, and the Rickert p.246 line in CANONICAL-METHODOLOGY-v9.md:86 against corpus/rhetorical_ontology/Rickert, Thomas - Ambient Rhetoric...pdf. Both check out. But in the same cache, master-citation-report-parsed.json:221 carries pdfium ligature loss ('fgures' for 'figures') in a Caston 2021 verbatim marked `"use": "in-text"`, and :176 silently rewrites White 1985's 'imagination (phantasia) is the process...' to 'phantasia is the process...' with no ellipsis while silently repairing the PDF's OCR damage ('pha11tastiko11') without recording either edit. The pipeline can verify quotations and does not.

— The pdfium ligature grep across ~5.5 MB and 391 files returned exactly 2 hits, and they are the same entry duplicated across the two runs. The hazard is real but extremely sparse here; a word-boundary regex over ~40 patterns is enough to find it, and that check costs nothing.

— GBAM's own text is the best witness against it. VALIDATION-v4-barfight.md:4 and v5:4 openly state that /tmp/rdr2-preflight/ 'was cleared by an overnight reboot' and that evidence was 'reproduced from the v3 validation doc'. CANONICAL-METHODOLOGY-v9.md's changelog records that two of its own artifacts still carry retired framing and that it chose not to fix them — and one of those two (ontological-wiring-A0-A4.md) is the single largest ingested document in the entry at 24 of 61 chunks. entries.granularity_gap: Finest unit ACTUALLY ENCODED is not the clip - it is the frame. The 68 raw-frame-logs address 1,040 distinct frames by id (e_0001, l_0385, q_101, ...) with 529 t=/t~ timestamps and 1,326 bullet-level observations, at 24 fps for 02:29-03:45. That is one to two levels BELOW the user's clause-level target on the temporal axis. Above it sit 284 timestamped beat rows in 22 beat-maps, then 32 element rows, then the prose syntheses. So the claim/clause-level material is not missing - it is already written, at roughly 69,080 words of it, and it is 100% unstructured: zero IDs, 24 header dialects, evidence-grade encoded in free text inside column headers ('inferred', 'NO dialogue anchor', '[UNCERTAIN]'), and the whole raw tier orphaned from the manifest. What would have to be ADDED is therefore not observation but a schema: a stable id per beat and per frame-observation, an explicit evidence-grade enum (frame-observed / subtitle-read / transcript-derived / role-inferred / author-confirmed / refuted), a supersedes/superseded-by edge so frame-read-verification.md's 10 verdicts attach to the 284 beat rows they judge, and a claim->quotation->locator triple so 'Oh, you struggled...' resolves to a frame id rather than a stitched paraphrase. Cost is extraction and normalisation, not new analysis - which materially lowers the price of the whole programme for this entry. The one thing genuinely absent is a claim-level decomposition of the entry's OWN argumentative prose (rdr2-tutorial-RODA.md's 5,135 words of sections 0-8 contain perhaps 80-120 discrete assertions with zero addressing).
strengths: frame-read-verification.md is the best falsification apparatus in the batch: 10 named claims, each with an explicit CONFIRMED / REFUTED / UNCLEAR / RESOLVED verdict and a finding, including three verdicts that go against the prior reading (:12 REFUTED gambling window, :14 not-Trelawney + honor not confirmed, :16 no bear maul). Honest, in-band uncertainty marking: 21 of 22 beat-maps say 'inferred' in the header; the gambling beat-map's :8 CRITICAL banner is a model of self-incrimination. The information exists - it is only mis-located (in headers and prose, not fields).

entries.verdict: Salvageable, and it is the single most valuable entry in this batch to salvage - but its current form is actively hazardous and it must be rebuilt as data rather than repaired as prose. The observation layer is outstanding: 1,040 frame-anchored observations, 284 timestamped beats, a genuine falsification pass and a genuine draft crosswalk. Nothing comparable exists elsewhere in corpus/index. But the entry has no mechanism by which a correction can reach the artefact it corrects, and the consequence is measurable: five refuted claims (bear-as-flinch at rdr2-element-matrix.md:57,89,90 and rdr2-vs-gg-differential.md:13,21; honor-active-on-bar-fight at rdr2-element-matrix.md:71, rdr2-tutorial-RODA.md:131, Bar Fight beatmap :27, Rape Scene beatmap :33) sit live in the highest-value chunks, one of them inside the §8 summary paragraph of the file the Part II plan names as its source. Judged against its own stated standard it fails - manifest.json:23 says the differential is 'done' when the file says it is a footage-independent draft; phase0-overview.md indexes 72 of 141 files and never names the ontological-change specimen; both repo-relative manifest paths are broken by a U+00D7-vs-x slip. Judged against the claim/clause-level target it is the strange case that is already BELOW target on granularity and simultaneously incapable of delivering it, because none of the 1,326 observations has an identifier, an evidence-grade field, or a supersession edge. And judged against reachability it is nowhere: 0 nodes in compiled-index.json and 0 rows in scripts/ingest/manifest.jsonl, so D4's promise of entry-scoped retrieval is currently fiction. Rebuild: keep every word, add ids + evidence-grade + supersedes edges + a claim->frame-id locator, register in TEXT_DIRS and in the ingest, and delete nothing.

entries.granularity_gap: This entry is the closest thing in the corpus to the user's target and it should be the template. vds-claims-moves.md already IS a claim-level index: 157 rows, each with a stable unique id (A-P01..A-C05, B-*, C-*; zero duplicates, verified), a terse statement, a thesis page or page-range, a tier, a reuse-disposition from a closed vocabulary (keep-verbatim / re-ground / enrich / supersede / drop), and one or more RODA anchors from a declared enum (A0-horizon, A1-perception, A2-phantasma, A3-doxa/emotion, A4-action/hexis, A4->A0', union(R1-R7), recalcitrance, rupture, hinge, VR<->2D, framing) plus a [V:...] volatility flag. Add vds-terminology.md (29 ids with type/origin/thesis_pp/RODA mapping), vds-interlocutor-loci.md (22 sources with per-source cited loci at page granularity - the Heidegger BT row alone lists ~30 discrete page loci - plus an explicit corpus_index_bridge column naming real sibling directories), and gg-element-matrix.md (54 ids across 6 typed blocks). That is 262 addressable rows over 15,481 words: roughly one structured claim per 59 words. Distance to target is therefore ONE step, not two: the unit is already the claim, not the chapter. What is missing is (a) clause-level decomposition inside each claim's evidence - the 'th p' column gives a page, never a quoted clause or a line locator, so no claim carries its own verbatim; (b) serialization - every row is a markdown pipe table, so the ids exist but nothing can dereference them; (c) edges - the anchors and the corpus_index_bridge column are latent typed relations (claim -> RODA locus, claim -> interlocutor, source -> sibling entry) that are stored as comma strings and never materialised. Extraction cost is low and mechanical: five tables, four of them single-dialect. The one genuine absence is that vds-claims-moves.md indexes the SOURCE thesis's claims, not the entry's own analytical claims - the 3,883 words of gg-RODA-matrix.md prose carry perhaps 150-200 further assertions with no addressing at all.
strengths: vds-claims-moves.md - 157 uniquely-ided, page-anchored claims with a closed disposition vocabulary and a closed RODA anchor enum. Verified: 157 rows, zero duplicate ids, declared count exactly right. This is the single best claim-level artifact found in this batch and should be the schema the whole index is rebuilt toward.

vds-interlocutor-loci.md - per-source loci at page granularity (the BT row enumerates ~30 distinct page anchors with parenthetical glosses), an explicit corpus_index_bridge column whose values are real sibling directory names (all tested: Heidegger - Being and Time, A Grammar of Motives (Burke 1945), A Rhetoric of Motives (Burke 1950), Von Uexkull - A Foray..., In-Game (Calleja 2011), Rickert - Ambient Rhetoric, Heidegger and Rhetoric - all exist), and a 'Citation-integrity flags' section that self-reports I-BAUDRILLARD as cited-but-absent-from-Works-Cited. That is a real, honest citation gate.

entries.verdict: Sound in conception, defective in bookkeeping, and structurally the most promotable entry in the batch - but it must be rebuilt as data. Judged against its own standard it is genuinely good: it declares a resolvable, ingested source with an explicit page-offset rule, it enumerates the thesis's sections, it self-audits its coverage of the five RODA pillars, it flags its own citation-integrity problem (Baudrillard), and it designed drift-isolation before it needed it. Judged against the claim/clause-level target it is the only entry in the batch already at claim granularity - 157 ided, page-anchored, dispositioned claims, one per ~59 words - and the redesign should take vds-claims-moves.md as its schema rather than inventing one. But the bookkeeping is failing in a specific and diagnostic way: three of five manifest counts are wrong (interlocutors 21 vs 22, elements 55 vs 54, episodes 2 vs 4), the manifest omits a file, phase0-overview.md's four cross-home pointers are all broken relative paths including the one marked 'Start here', and a correction pass that overturned the entry's headline footage claim was recorded in one file while three others - manifest.json:22, gg-frame-trace.md:72, gg-element-matrix.md:33 - still certify the refuted reading as 'confirmed', with the correcting file's own frame archive now vanished. That is the same one-directional-correction failure as the RDR2 entry, from the same root cause: no ids on the corrected rows, so a correction can only be written as a new document. 'No synthesis layer' is a defensible design decision for an analysis-artifact - this entry genuinely has nothing external to synthesise - but it has been used to excuse the absence of any structured layer at all, and the result is 0 nodes in compiled-index.json and 0 chunks in ChromaDB while the raw thesis PDF it decomposes is fully searchable. Do not rebuild the analysis; serialize it, wire the latent edges, fix five counts and five paths, and register it.

Neither entry has multiple external sources to synthesise across (RDR2 = one playthrough; Veri(dis) = one thesis), so the absence of a _synthesis/ directory is correct. What is NOT justified is that the decision was allowed to mean "no structured layer at all." Both entries then reinvented, in prose, the two things a synthesis layer exists to provide — a cross-cutting concept register and a supersession record — and both reinventions failed in the identical way (see below). RDR2 in fact HAS synthesis artifacts (rdr2-element-matrix.md, rdr2-tutorial-RODA.md, rdr2-vs-gg-differential.md, frame-read-verification.md); they are simply flat-filed and unnamed as such.

"whether the .vtt transcripts are indexable content being thrown away" — YES, and with a serious caveat that cuts both ways. They are thrown away: 0 rows in the ingest manifest, 44 files (22 .vtt + 22 .txt) of primary dialogue. But they should NOT be ingested as-is. Measured: 8 of 22 .txt files are 100% whisper hallucination noise tokens (08, 09, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, "5 finger intro" — the manifest's caveat at :19 names only 6 of those 8, omitting clip 12 and 5-finger). "RDR2 - 5 finger intro.txt" is 40 bytes of "you" repeated ten times. "RDR2 - 1 - Opening Cinematic.txt" carries 7 of its 80 lines as "(c) transcript Emily Beynon" — a hallucinated third-party copyright credit that would function as a fabricated attribution if retrieved and quoted, and which is flagged only in a different file (that clip's beat-map, :7). "RDR2 - Rape Scene.vtt" additionally uses MM:SS.mmm timestamps where the other 21 use HH:MM:SS.mmm. The right answer is: ingest the ~14 clean transcripts with per-cue timestamp anchors, quarantine the 8 noise files behind an explicit evidence-grade field, and repair the two known verbatim errors ("his mind" -> "its mind"; strip the Beynon credit) — not ingest the folder wholesale.

THE CROSS-ENTRY FINDING THAT MATTERS MOST

Both entries independently ran a second, higher-fidelity verification pass that overturned their own earlier findings — RDR2's frame-read-verification.md (2026-06-27, 10 verdicts, 3 refutations) and Veri(dis)'s gg-e6-dense-trace.md (2026-06-26, 2 fps re-read of the tavern). RDR2 — 0 of 22 beat-maps contain the string "frame-read-verification" (grep -ln, zero hits), while that log's :23 lists "CORRECTIONS to fold in" and :29 claims "The beat-maps for clips 9 and 12 are corrected by this log" — a correction never written. Five refuted claims remain live: rdr2-element-matrix.md:57,:71,:89,:90 and rdr2-vs-gg-differential.md:13,:21. One file contradicts itself across 97 lines (rdr2-tutorial-RODA.md:34 "honor INERT ... author-confirmed" vs :131 "active on socially-witnessed excess (clip 10's bar-fight, Trelawney's ...)"), and the wrong version is the one in the §8 summary paragraph — the highest-retrieval-value chunk in the entry.

Veri(dis) — gg-frame-trace.md contains 0 hits for "dense" though gg-e6-dense-trace.md:3 declares it "Supersedes the 1 fps coverage of E6". The refuted 08:51/f534 + 08:52/f537 reading survives in three places (manifest.json:22, gg-frame-trace.md:72 under a header reading "Discrepancies — RESOLVED", gg-element-matrix.md:33 labelled "footage-confirmed") against one corrected place (gg-RODA-matrix.md:86) — and that same file then re-certifies it at :141.

Worse, the evidence asymmetry runs backwards: Veri(dis)'s superseded 1 fps archive is fully preserved (897 jpgs at tmp/Dissertation/Part_II/Part-II-GG-Repurpose/gg-frames, count matching manifest.json:18 exactly), while the superseding 2 fps archive declared at gg-e6-dense-trace.md:3 as "scratchpad/gg-e6-dense/" does not exist anywhere in the repo. Same pattern in RDR2: 65 references to /tmp/claude-1000/-home-dalton-projects-claudeflow-testing/8b6ba3ed-.../scratchpad/rape-scene/logs/ resolve to nothing.

This is the same failure the prior audit found between per-source and _synthesis edge CSVs — "the same data serialized twice, and nothing records which is stale" — appearing here in prose. It is not a CSV problem. It is the absence of row-level identity plus a supersedes edge, and it will reappear in any redesign that adds ids without adding that edge.

WHAT SURPRISED ME

The granularity finding inverts the batch's framing. The brief treats these as low-value analysis-artifacts. In fact RDR2 contains the finest-grained material anywhere in corpus/index — 1,040 distinct frame ids, 1,731 frame citations, 529 timestamped observations, 1,326 bullet-level records across 68 files, at 24 fps for the 02:29–03:45 event window. That is BELOW clause level on the temporal axis, already written, 69,080 words of it — and the entire directory is orphaned: grep -rn "raw-frame-logs" across the entry (excluding self-references) returns zero, and phase0-overview.md returns zero hits for "rape" or "Sonny". A manifest-driven cleanup would delete 57% of the entry's markdown without noticing. Meanwhile Veri(dis)'s vds-claims-moves.md is already a 157-row, uniquely-ided, page-anchored, closed-vocabulary claim index at roughly one structured claim per 59 words — the schema the whole programme is trying to reach, sitting unregistered in a markdown pipe table.

So for these two entries the claim-level programme is not a data-collection problem. It is an extraction-and-serialization problem, and the cost estimate for them should drop sharply. The genuinely missing pieces are narrow and identical across both: a stable id per row, an evidence-grade enum (frame-observed / subtitle-read / transcript-derived / role-inferred / author-confirmed / refuted) to replace the free-text uncertainty glosses currently hidden in column headers, a supersedes/superseded-by edge, and a claim -> verbatim -> locator triple so that quotations like "Oh, you struggled..." resolve to a frame id instead of, as at rdr2-rape-scene-RODA.md:118, being certified "CONFIRMED verbatim (subtitles + whisper)" when the cited whisper source (transcripts/RDR2 - Rape Scene.vtt:70) actually reads "You struggle and you lost but it was quite a tussle.
