entries.granularity_gap: The finest unit the entry FORMALLY encodes is the chapter/section unit (fcm-00..fcm-14, one per FCM chapter or section group). But claim-level material is already present in bulk, unstructured or semi-structured, and this materially changes the cost of the programme. Quantified: (a) 182 records in 'claims' arrays across 13 unit JSONs, each with id + a one-sentence proposition + a triple locus - e.g. fcm-05 C2 'Depth, not objective span of time, decides the extent of boredom; one can be more bored in five minutes of company than in four hours at the station.' with locus '(p.108 / GA pp.163-64 / pdf 66)'. That is already claim-level with page-precise anchoring. (b) 63 further records in 'objects' arrays in fcm-07/08/09. (c) The units' 'sections' arrays go one level finer still - subsection records like §25b 'Obstructive casualness (Lassigkeit) as the deepening way we are left empty' with book_p 116, giving a section-to-subsection tree beneath each unit. (d) 1,083 inline triple-loci across the 26 markdown files and 2,090 quoted spans in the unit prose - each locus marks a specific quotation or claim, so the prose already carries clause-anchored evidence, just as text rather than records. So roughly 245 structured claim records + ~1,100 locus-anchored prose claims are ALREADY authored. What is missing is (i) stable claim IDs that edges can point at - today edges point at free-text concept names, never at C1/C2; (ii) a uniform claims key (fcm-08/09 use 'objects'); (iii) any clause-level decomposition (no entry file segments a claim into subject/predicate/qualifier or marks the specific clause a locus certifies); and (iv) any path from claim records to runtime. To reach claim-level the honest work is normalization and wiring, not authoring. To reach clause-level, genuinely new work is required across all 15 units.
strengths: Provenance discipline is the best thing here and must survive any redesign: FAITHFUL-HEIDEGGER / FAITHFUL-EMPIRICAL / PROJECTED are kept strictly separate, declared at manifest.json:65 and enforced as a column in every edge CSV (440 faithful vs 11 anticipatory-application). The King-Salvo bridge md opens with a 'Provenance discipline (read first)' block and tags every mapping PROJECTED.

Triple-locus citation convention (book / GA / pdf) applied 1,083 times in prose and 662 times in edge CSVs, with an explicit verification document (page-offset-verification.md) giving the 2-up formula, six empirical running-head anchors, and the exact pdftotext column-split commands used.
182 claim records with ids and loci in the unit JSONs - genuinely claim-level content that already exists and only needs wiring.

Uniform edge CSV dialect: all 16 edge files share one header (source,relation,target,locus,provenance,note) and one 16-term relation vocabulary with no drift between per-unit and synthesis layers - unusually disciplined for this corpus.
Honest gate reporting where it fails: bibliography_min_120 is recorded as 'RELAXED -> 49 (honest interlocutor count for a lecture course; padding would fabricate figures)' rather than faked.

Section 6 of the King-Salvo bridge ('A category caution') explicitly refuses the overclaim that a 17-minute Word tutorial induces Heideggerian profound boredom, and states which transfers are structural vs analogical. That epistemic caution is the load-bearing asset for Part III.

The three bridge-source digests carry reliability flags per finding ([clean], [suggestive], [inconclusive], [statistically significant]) and record the papers' own limits (EEG N=1-clean; 'learning' never measured despite the title).
No stub or near-empty files; no ligature corruption (targeted grep for benefcial/identifed/specifc/frst etc. returned only legitimate words).
entries.verdict: Salvageable, and the most craftsmanlike entry I have seen in this corpus - but structurally incapable of the stated goal without a rebuild of its wiring. By its own standard (a) it is close to excellent: the manifest's counts are almost all true (units 15 = 15, global_edges 452 = 452, terminology 150 = 150, german 66 = 66, bibliography 49 = 49, concept_matrix_rows 45 = 45, ontology_nodes_registered 32 = 32, tension_edges 7 = 7), the source PDF resolves, the provenance layering is real and enforced in data, and the triple-locus convention is applied consistently. Only two of its eight self-declared gates actually fail (no_verbatim_over_25w, and triple_loci at 21% inconsistency), plus three metric slips (deep_md_words, edges_faithful, the malformed CSV row). Against goal (b) it is structurally incapable as built: the entry's unit is a chapter, its 880 edges point at free text rather than ids, its four identifier namespaces do not join, and 98%+ of its authored content - including all 245 claim records and the entire King-Salvo bridge - reaches runtime not at all. Crucially, the claim-level content is already written; what is missing is a claim-ID namespace, a single edge endpoint vocabulary, and a compiler that reads more than one markdown section. I would keep every byte of the prose, the digests, the locus apparatus and the provenance tags, and rebuild the identifier and registration layer around the existing 'claims' arrays. Do not rebuild from scratch: the expensive part is done.

entries.granularity_gap: The finest formally-encoded unit is the essay (or half-essay: Gross is split A/B at book p.27). That is one level coarser than a chapter in FCM terms. But substantial claim-level material already exists inside the phase-2 records: 74 'positions' across the 8 units (each an essay-level proposition with an id such as HR-01-GROSS-A-P2 and a page anchor), 146 key_concepts, 69 tensions/open questions, 233 local edges, and - unusually - two loci concordances that are already sub-claim-level: hr-heidegger-loci-concordance.json holds 162 distinct Heidegger loci and hr-aristotle-loci-concordance.json holds 66 Aristotle loci, each with the citing contributor, the essay page and a context field. Several of those context fields are already clause-anchored: e.g. the GA 18 262 entry reproduces the full English and German block quotation with the note 'This is the volume's most-cited single GA 18 quote'. The eight phase-2 markdown analyses (~44,000 words) and the 7 contested-node dossiers plus 11 disagreement dossiers carry a further dense layer of claim-level argument in prose, each keyed to a contributor and a page. So the claim layer is roughly half-built and, unlike FCM, it is already ID-bearing (POSITION:HR-NN-AUTHOR-Pn). Three things block it: (1) 14 of those position ids were never resolved (TBD/-Pn/-P[...]); (2) positions live only in phase-2 JSON and never appear in the ontology, the matrix or compiled-index; (3) the POSITION ids and the CONCEPT labels use different, non-joining vocabularies. Clause-level is entirely absent - nothing in the entry decomposes a position into its constituent clauses or marks which clause a given GA-18 locus certifies. Cost implication: getting HR to claim level is mostly ID hygiene and wiring; getting it to clause level is new authoring across 8 essays and ~230 loci.
strengths: The inter-contributor disagreement apparatus is genuinely rare and must be preserved: inter-contributor-disagreements.json (11 dossiers DG1-DG11, count declared 11 and actually 11), tension-edges.json (12 volume tensions VT1-VT12 with dependency AND conflict edges plus a synthesis paragraph each), and contested-nodes.md (7 dossiers with per-contributor reading tables and 'categorial consequence' columns). Nothing else in the corpus maps a scholarly debate at this resolution.

Two loci concordances with real sub-claim granularity: 162 Heidegger loci and 66 Aristotle loci, each with citing contributor, essay page, and context; 26 of them carry resolvable bridge paths into the BT and BCAP entries.

Consistent ID-prefix discipline in the edge layer: 265 distinct endpoints, every one prefixed (CONCEPT / HEIDEGGER-LOCUS / POSITION / ARISTOTLE-LOCUS / INTERLOCUTOR / BCAP-LOCUS). This is far better than FCM's zero-prefix free text and is the right base to normalize onto.

An edge_domain column (rhetorical 65, ontological 40, political 30, philological 17, hermeneutic 14, ethical 14, existential 9, methodological 7, genealogical 4, temporal 4) - a facet no other layer in the batch provides.
Node definitions are substantive (355-901 chars, mean ~610) and comparative rather than dictionary-style: each names which contributors hold which reading and where they disagree.

Bibliographic and OCR provenance: pdf_page_offset 6 with 11 confirmed landmarks, per-essay pdf ranges, per-essay ocr_confidence, and specific ocr_alerts (Hyde 'PDF p.100 is rotated 180 degrees in source PDF'; Poggeler 'PDF p.169 shows right-edge column-2 truncation').

A philological variant is recorded as a first-class disagreement: Gross siding with the Bröcker transcript ('aristotelischen Rhetorik') against Michalski/Schalk ('aristotelischen Logic') at GA 18 110, captured in inter-contributor-disagreements.json:258 and :352 and in the .md at :136.
No stub files, no JSON parse failures, no ligature corruption (targeted grep clean).
entries.verdict: Salvageable in substance, but the wiring and the bookkeeping need rebuilding. Judged by its own stated standard the entry fails repeatedly: its manifest says phase 1 is in progress and phases 2-3 pending while all of phase 2 and 24 phase-3 artifacts sit on disk; its ontology declares 33 nodes in four places and has 36; its tier headers say 12/16 and the tables have 14/19; its interlocutor map declares 21/23 and holds 20/25; its contested set is declared as 6 three times with three different memberships; and 14 position IDs were shipped as TBD placeholders. The two edge layers cannot be reconciled - only 91 of 233 per-unit edges match a synthesis row exactly, 149 after normalization, leaving 83 authored edges dropped without record. Judged against the claim/clause-level target it is structurally incapable as built: the unit is a whole essay, every node reaches runtime with units: [], and three identifier dialects for the same 36 concepts mean nothing joins to anything. Yet the intellectual content is the best argument-mapping in the corpus - 11 disagreement dossiers, 12 volume tensions with both dependency and conflict edges, 7 contested-concept dossiers, 228 concordance loci, and 74 already-ID'd positions. The right move is not a rebuild from scratch but a normalization pass: resolve the 14 placeholder IDs, collapse the three concept dialects onto the POSITION-style prefixed namespace, promote positions to first-class records, add a units field to the node sections, and make the synthesis edge layer a derived artifact rather than a hand-retyped one. Then rewrite the manifest to describe what actually exists.

result.batch_notes:
PRIOR-CLAIM VERDICTS (tested against this batch only)

1. "~310 unit records, 691 unit analyses, ~9,762 distinct edges on disk; ZERO reach runtime." — PARTIAL. The "zero reach runtime" is FALSE as stated for whole entries: both entries DO put content in compiled-index.json (FCM 32 nodes + 7 tensionEdges; HR 36 nodes + 12 tensionEdges). It is EXACTLY TRUE for edges: 0 of FCM's 880 edge rows and 0 of HR's 437 edge records reach runtime. The claim should be restated as "no edge layer reaches runtime", which is precise and defensible.

2. "The compiler reads only 4 filename patterns plus tension-edges.json." — CONFIRMED by reading scripts/compile-corpus-index.py:1180-1272. collect_ontology_nodes opens book-level-ontology.md, falls back to cluster-ontology.md, and for Aristotle globs *-ontology.md; collect_cross_pipeline_hooks globs *-cross-pipeline-hooks.md in the Aristotle directory only; collect_tension_edges opens tension-edges.json. There is no csv import and no *.mmd or *.json glob anywhere else. Both entries in this batch are served solely by book-level-ontology.md + tension-edges.json.

3. "42 distinct edge-CSV header dialects, 633 distinct relation values, 31 unenforced ID prefixes." — PARTIAL/CONFIRMED in shape. This batch contributes 4 CSV headers (FCM: source,relation,target,locus,provenance,note across all 16 edge files, plus a concept-matrix header; HR: source,relation,edge_domain,target,note,contributors,unit_pages plus a concept-matrix header). Relation vocabularies are 16 (FCM, kebab-case: defines, contests, grounds-question, glosses-german, deepens-into, bridges-to-pipeline, temporalizes-as, interprets-experiment-finding, marginal-note...) and 15 (HR, snake_case: operationalizes, is_meaning_of, contrasts_with, presupposes, supports, refines, explains, exemplifies, undermines, historicizes, depends_on, supersedes, complexifies, is_presupposed_by, is_undermined_by). The two sets have ZERO overlap. ID prefixes: HR uses 6 in the CSV (CONCEPT, HEIDEGGER-LOCUS, POSITION, ARISTOTLE-LOCUS, INTERLOCUTOR, BCAP-LOCUS) plus a one-off BT-LOCUS in a phase-2 JSON; FCM uses NONE — 481 free-text endpoints, 463 of which resolve to nothing.

4. "Only ~10 manifests record source PDFs; 9 entries have NO machine-readable source path." — REFUTED for this batch. Both entries record a source PDF in manifest.json and both resolve on disk. HR additionally declares 8 essay file paths (all resolve) and 26 cross-entry bridge paths (all resolve). FCM's weakness is different: its 7 declared working-text paths point at /tmp/fcm-text/, which no longer exists, and the three King-Salvo papers that carry the bridge are named bibliographically only although they sit at corpus/Virtual Learning Environments/.

5. "Only 2 of 27 entries have a quality-gates-report.md; only 1 has machine-readable metrics." — PARTIAL/CONFIRMED. Neither entry has a quality-gates-report.md file. FCM's manifest.json DOES carry both a machine-readable `metrics` block (10 figures) and a `quality_gates` block (8 named gates with PASS/RELAXED verdicts) — FCM is plausibly the "1 with machine-readable metrics". HR's manifest has neither, and does not even list its 24 synthesis artifacts.

6. "ig-10-incorporation.json is the only unparseable JSON of 494." — CONFIRMED for this batch: all 18 FCM JSONs and all 25 HR JSONs parse with json.loads. Zero failures.

7. "4 of 11 tension-edges.json files yield ZERO edges silently." — REFUTED for this batch. FCM's is a bare list of 7 with node_a/node_b/dependency_edge.relation/conflict_edge.relation → 7/7 normalize. HR's is a dict whose "tensions" key is unwrapped by the parser → 12/12 normalize. compiled-index.json shows exactly 7 and 12.

8. "67 .mmd files across 15 entries encode 1,544 arrow-edges reachable by nothing." — CONFIRMED for this batch's share. FCM has 0 .mmd. HR has 5 encoding 124 arrows (25+23+34+22+20), read by nothing. hr-graph-global.mmd:2 even self-describes as "28 of 36 canonical nodes; ~37 load-bearing edges (of 204)".

9. "144 cross_pipeline_bridges live in 22 unit JSONs; runtime has 72 hooks, 100% Aristotle." — CONFIRMED on the runtime side: compiled-index.json has exactly 72 crossPipelineHooks and every sourceText is an Aristotle work. HR alone contributes 73 cross_pipeline_links (on 34 of 36 nodes in book-level-ontology.json) that reach nothing, so the 144 figure is if anything an undercount.

10. "35 *-deep.json files carry positions/tensions/interlocutors with no canonical slot." — NOT APPLICABLE to this batch; neither entry has a *-deep.json. But the pattern recurs under different filenames: HR's 8 phase2-*.json carry exactly that payload (74 positions, 146 key_concepts, 69 tensions, 174 interlocutor records, 233 edges) with no canonical slot.

11. "FCM 428 vs 452 disagreement; nothing records which is stale." — REFUTED on the diagnosis, CONFIRMED on the symptom. Neither layer is stale. Exact triple-set comparison: per-unit edges absent from global = 0. Global-only = 24, and they are a coherent class — cross-unit spine edges (fcm-04 deepens-into fcm-05, fcm-05→fcm-06, fcm-06 grounds-question fcm-08, fcm-08 extends fcm-09, fcm-09 extends fcm-13) plus 6 King-Salvo bridge edges (boredom-form-2 interprets-experiment-finding king-salvo-clinical-EEG-boring-vs-gaze-engaged; hingehaltenheit interprets-experiment-finding king-salvo-time-dilation; boredom-form-2 bridges-to-pipeline surface-depth-disagreement-index; and three others). global-edges.csv is a strict superset. The real defect is that NOTHING on disk states this relation, so a rebuild harvesting per-unit CSVs would silently delete the entire cross-unit spine and the Part-III-load-bearing bridge edges. I recommend correcting the register entry.

BRIEF ASSERTIONS TESTED

- "FCM: 61 files, 15 units, 880 edge rows" — ALL CONFIRMED exactly (61 files: md 26 / json 18 / csv 17; fcm-00..fcm-14 = 15; 428 + 452 = 880).
- "FCM DISAGREES between edge layers 428 vs 452" — CONFIRMED as arithmetic, REFUTED as staleness (see 11).
- "Heidegger and Rhetoric: 49 files, 16 units, 204 edge rows against 36 nodes" — CONFIRMED on files (49: json 25 / md 17 / mmd 5 / csv 2), CONFIRMED on 204 rows and 36 nodes. "16 units" is a double-count: there are 8 units (7 essays with Gross split A/B), each with one phase-1 and one phase-2 JSON record. The brief's own 204-vs-36 framing understates the problem — there are a further 233 edge records inside the phase-2 JSONs that the 204 does not include.
- "FCM carries the King-Salvo boredom bridge, load-bearing for Part III" — CONFIRMED and it is the best-written artifact in the batch, but it has two structural exposures: (a) six of its bridge edges exist ONLY in _synthesis/global-edges.csv, not in any per-unit file; (b) the two units it rests on, fcm-04 (first form) and fcm-05 (second form), have the worst locus integrity in the entry — 55.9% and 40.6% of their triple-loci are inconsistent with the manifest's own "verified" page-offset formula. A Part III citation drawn from those units needs re-verification against the PDF before use.

CROSS-ENTRY OBSERVATIONS

- The two entries fail in mirror-image ways, and each has what the other lacks. FCM has disciplined edge serialization (one header, one relation vocabulary, provenance column, triple loci) but zero ID discipline (481 free-text endpoints, four non-joining namespaces). HR has good ID discipline (6 prefixes, 265 prefixed endpoints, POSITION ids of the form HR-NN-AUTHOR-Pn) but two irreconcilable edge layers and no per-unit CSV at all. A redesign should take FCM's serialization and HR's namespace.
- Both entries independently invented a "§3A Canonical Node List" section appended after their real content, explicitly labelled as harvest bait for the compiler (FCM book-level-ontology.md:64 "Registration-format node list (harvested by scripts/compile-corpus-index.py)"; HR :151 the same). This is the tell that the authors knew the compiler reads only one section and hand-fed it. Everything else in both entries was written for a reader, not the machine.
- Claim-level material is already extensive and this changes the cost model: FCM has 182 id'd claims + 63 objects with triple loci, and 1,083 inline loci across its prose; HR has 74 id'd positions, 228 concordance loci with contributor and page, plus 18 debate dossiers. Neither reaches runtime. The expensive authoring is largely done; what is missing is a claim-ID namespace, a single endpoint vocabulary, and a compiler that reads more than one markdown heading.
- Neither entry shows any pdfium ligature corruption. I grepped both for benefcial / identifed / specifc / signifcant / difcult / frst / feld / confrm / defne / refect / fnd / ofer / sufer and every hit was a legitimate word ("beneficial", "identifies", "effects", "Bedeutung"). The scanned-PDF hazard did not reach these two entries.
- Neither entry contains a stub or near-empty file. Smallest files are 1,575 bytes (HR concept-matrix.csv) and 2,110 bytes (FCM page-offset-verification.md), both substantive.
- The compiler's deduplicate_ontology_nodes (scripts/compile-corpus-index.py:1311-1348) is a corpus-wide hazard this batch exposes clearly: it merges by lowercased name across ALL texts and keeps only the longer definition. FCM loses its own definitions for Profound boredom, Langeweile, Dasein and logos; HR loses its own for Pathos, Enthymeme, Logos, Rhetoric, Resoluteness and Destruktion. Ten authored definitions in this batch alone are silently replaced at compile time by another entry's text, with only a semicolon-joined `text` string as evidence that anything happened. Any redesign must make merge non-destructive.

entries.granularity_gap: Finest structured unit = the CHAPTER (14 units). Everything registered at runtime is coarser still: 56 book-level concepts. But claim-level material is ALREADY PRESENT in structured form and simply has no canonical slot. Concretely, on disk right now: 101 unit-level `positions`, 94 of them dicts, of which the well-formed ones look exactly like claim records — gm-00-deep.json positions[] carry {id: 'P-AMBIGUITY-AS-RESOURCE', claim: '<one-sentence proposition>', book_page: 18, critique_target: '<who it argues against>', centrality_tier: 1}; 48 of the 101 are page-anchored. Add 12 more book-level POSITIONs each with a `claim` field (book-level-ontology.json:593 shows the shape). Add 70 unit-level `tensions`, each a named contested proposition-pair (35 page-anchored), plus 16 canonical tensions and 21 unmatched raw tensions with per-unit provenance. Add 441 concept records (290 page-anchored) with paraphrastic definitions. Add 139 `outline` entries which are SUB-CHAPTER sections with book_pp/pdf_pp ranges and multi-sentence summaries — i.e. one granularity level below chapter already exists and is page-ranged. So the entry is roughly ONE level short of the target on the structured side, not two: chapter → section (139 outline records, exists) → claim (113 position records, exists but heterogeneous) → clause (does not exist anywhere). The clause level is entirely absent: nothing on disk carries a sentence offset, a character span, or a bbox; the finest locator is a book page number. On the unstructured side the raw material is dense — 59,379 words / ~2,485 sentences of unit prose plus 39,356 words of synthesis prose, page-anchored throughout — from which claim extraction is a parsing problem, not an authoring problem. What would have to be added: (1) a canonical claim record type with a stable ID, a normalised page+paragraph or char-span locator, a provenance tag, and edges to the concepts it involves; (2) normalisation of the 101 existing positions (7 are bare strings, 40 lack a prefixed ID, 53 lack a page) into that type; (3) a compiler slot so claims and tensions reach compiled-index.json at all — today neither does. Cost is materially lower than a rebuild because the hard scholarly work (reading 518 pages, anchoring claims to pages) is done.
strengths: The manifest is the best in this batch and probably a template worth generalising: verified page-offset formula with a 15-landmark verification table quoting the exact extracted header at each landmark, machine-run per-philosopher cite_check with hit counts and unique-page counts, a documented OCR artefact inventory, per-unit role/edge_target/triple_pass flags, and 14 folder paths that all resolve.

concept-matrix.csv is provably consistent with book-level-ontology.json: all 56 concept_ids match exactly (0 in either direction), and for all 56 rows the count of marked unit cells equals the declared total_units_appearing AND equals the ontology's first_introduced_unit ∪ developed_across_units set. Zero drift. This is the only cross-artefact consistency in the entry that fully holds.

canonical-id-resolution-report.md is genuine engineering documentation: it names the 8 CSV header dialects, explains the adaptive header-mapper, and states the 878→876 reduction with the reason (2 duplicate triples merged). I verified both numbers independently — per-unit rows sum to exactly 878, pre-canonical has exactly 2 duplicate (source,relation,target) triples, global has 0, and the two files' triple sets are identical. The layers are consistent and the discrepancy is recorded.

contested-nodes.md is the strongest debate-mapping artefact I have seen in this corpus: 10 contested concepts with a five-part taxonomy of contestation types (multiple definitions / register-shift / circumference drift / reference instability / dramatistic-load mismatch), cross-volume frequency, enumerated senses with page anchors, an explicit statement of Burke's own posture, and a dissertation-leverage assessment.

OCR hazard is documented rather than hidden: manifest.json's ocr_audit_summary and five per-unit ocr_notes fields name the exact italic-tl artefacts ('explicidy', 'sufficiendy', 'elementaiism', 'Cariolanus', 'std' for 'stā') and flag the chapters at risk, and no corrupted string leaked into authored prose.

The 139 `outline` records are sub-chapter sections with both book and PDF page ranges plus substantive summaries — a genuine intermediate granularity layer that any redesign should keep rather than re-derive.

gm-terminology-appendix.json (347 lemmas), gm-philosophers-cited-concordance.json (83 philosophers), gm-bibliography-extracted.json (196 publications reconstructed from footnotes and Index for a volume with no reference list), and gm-interlocutor-map.json (35 tiered interlocutors) are substantial, non-stub, exceeded-target artefacts.
entries.verdict: SALVAGEABLE, and the most valuable single entry in this batch — but its runtime footprint is a rounding error against what it contains. The scholarship is excellent by its own standard: the manifest, the offset verification, the cite-check, the concept-matrix/ontology consistency, and contested-nodes.md are the work of a careful pipeline that mostly did what its plan told it to. What failed is everything downstream of authoring. The single canonical-ID pass the entry itself declares 'required before downstream dissertation deployment' was never run, so 876 edges carry resolution_status 'heuristic-pending-3A' and only 13 of 963 endpoints are real IDs. The tension file was written in a schema the compiler cannot read, so 37 tension records vanish without a warning. The 12 POSITION nodes — the volume's actual claims — were never mirrored into the markdown the compiler reads. Six units mis-report their own edge counts and two falsely certify content-filter compliance that their prose twins falsify in 31 places. And none of the 91 files is in git. Against the claim/clause target the entry is structurally incapable as it stands — there is no clause-level locator anywhere and no compiler slot for a claim — but it is NOT far from claim level: 113 claim-shaped records and 139 section-level records already exist with page anchors, and 2,485 sentences of page-anchored prose sit behind them. The right move is not a rebuild but a normalisation-plus-registration pass: fix the tension schema, run the deferred 3A canonicalisation, promote positions/tensions to first-class registered types, add a claim record with a sub-page locator, and put the whole thing under version control. Rebuilding would destroy the manifest and contested-nodes work, which is the part that is genuinely hard to reproduce.

CROSS-ENTRY OBSERVATIONS

A. NEITHER ENTRY IS IN GIT. Zero of 91 Grammar files and zero of 35 Rhetoric files are tracked; `git check-ignore` finds no rule, so they are simply untracked ('??'), while 335 other files under corpus/index ARE tracked. This is the highest-severity finding in the batch and I suspect it is not confined to these two entries — it should be checked corpus-wide before any redesign touches anything.

B. THE TWO ENTRIES ARE INVERSE FAILURES, AND THE FIX IS TO CROSS-BREED THEM. Grammar has world-class apparatus (manifest with 15-landmark offset verification and a machine-run cite-check; a 56×14 concept-matrix that is provably 100% consistent with its ontology; contested-nodes.md; a canonical-id-resolution-report) sitting on top of an undisciplined edge layer (398 relations, 280 singletons, 98.6% unresolved endpoints, 8 header dialects, 100% of rows stuck at resolution_status 'heuristic-pending-3A'). Rhetoric has a world-class edge layer (10 relations declared in advance and honoured, 0 singletons, 0 empty cells, binary provenance) with almost no apparatus (no manifest, no matrix, no tension file, no resolution report). Grammar's discipline problem is that its spec was written per-agent; Rhetoric's phase0-overview.md declared the schema and the closed vocabulary BEFORE the work and the agents obeyed. That is the reproducible lesson.

C. CLAIM-LEVEL MATERIAL ALREADY EXISTS AND IS CHEAPER THAN EXPECTED. Across the batch: 154 `positions` records (101 GM + 53 RM), the Rhetoric ones uniformly {id, claim, book_page, provenance} with 47/53 page-anchored; 12 more book-level POSITIONs in Grammar's ontology JSON with a `claim` field; 223 `outline` records that are SECTION-level with book and PDF page ranges; 103 tensions. The claim tier is not missing — it is unregistered and, on the Grammar side, heterogeneously typed. What is genuinely absent corpus-wide is the CLAUSE tier: nothing in either entry carries a sentence index, character offset or bbox; the finest locator anywhere is a book page number. Any clause-level programme therefore needs a new locator primitive, whereas the claim-level programme mostly needs a schema and a compiler slot.

D. TWO SILENT DEGRADATION MODES WORTH GENERALISING. (i) Self-certification fields that are simply false — Grammar's gm-01-deep.json:339 and gm-07-deep.json:410 both certify no ≥25-word Burke verbatim, and both are falsified by their own .md twins (52 and 44 words). A compliance sweep reading those fields reports PASS. (ii) The ChromaDB copy of the ONE file the compiler reads is stale in BOTH entries — the manifest sha256 for each `_synthesis/book-level-ontology.md` no longer matches disk, and the drift is precisely the appended '## 3A. Canonical Node List' registration block, so the vector store holds the pre-registration text in both cases.

E. CONTENT-FILTER BREACHES ARE REAL AND MEASURABLE. Both pipelines mandate "no ≥25-word verbatim from Burke" (plans/grammar-of-motives-burke-1945-analysis.md:247 and :392; Rhetoric's phase0-overview.md "## Content filter (MANDATORY)"). A properly paired-quote scan finds 31 breaches in Grammar (max 97 words, gm-10-deep.md:21) and 5 in Rhetoric (max 81 words, rm-07-deep.md:58). Methodological warning for anyone repeating this: a naive `"([^"]+)"` regex produces ~1,700 false positives per entry by pairing a closing quote with the next opening quote and by matching whole JSON string values. Line-scoped alternating-split on the quote character is the only reliable method I found.

F. WHAT SURPRISED ME. Grammar's manifest.json is not boilerplate — its cite_check block contains empirically derived findings that changed the analysis ("TIER-A INTERLOCUTOR SURPRISE: Korzybski (36 hits, 19 pages) is unexpectedly central; Plan §2.1 + §4.1 do not pre-flag Korzybski") and its non_blocking_advisories correctly record that a referenced pipeline does not exist ("Hawhee Moving Bodies pipeline does not exist in corpus/index/ — plan §1.4 reference must be updated"). That is a manifest doing real epistemic work. It makes the surrounding failures more frustrating, not less: the pipeline was capable of this level of rigour and still shipped six units with wrong edge counts, an unreadable tension file, and no version control.

entries.granularity_gap: The finest STRUCTURED unit is the analysis unit — a Metaphysics book, a Physics book, or a De Anima chapter-group (34 units over 553 PDF pages, i.e. ~16 pages per unit; the analyses run 1,147-5,332 words each). That is two levels above the target. BUT claim-level and clause-level material is ALREADY AUTHORED, in bulk, inside the prose, and that changes the economics of the whole programme. Quantified over the 34 phase2-*.md (158,205 words): 1,539 bullets, of which 973 carry an explicit Bekker locus (63% — roughly 29 addressable claims per unit); 2,323 DISTINCT Bekker loci with line numbers (e.g. `429a1–2`, `431a14–17`); 1,594 quoted strings of 25+ characters; 1,891 markdown table rows; and 129 already-IDed propositions under a `UNIT-NN-Pn` convention (156 distinct IDs referenced) in 20 of the 34 files. Add 188 bekker-index loci each already bound to a concept list and a unit_id, and 164 Greek lemmas with 1,000+ citation strings. Crucially, Bekker line numbers ARE the canonical clause-level address system for Aristotle, and this entry already records them at that resolution — so the corpus is not missing clause-level ADDRESSES, it is missing (a) IDs on the ~844 unIDed claim bullets, (b) any JSON serialization of any of it, (c) trustworthy page/offset anchors (see the CRITICAL locator defects — the JSON layer's pdf_pages are wrong by up to 47 pages while the prose layer's are verified correct), and (d) character offsets into the extracted text for span-level retrieval. What would have to be added: a per-claim record {claim_id, unit_id, bekker_locus, verified_pdf_page, char_span, claim_text, quoted_evidence, relation_edges[], tension_refs[]}, minted by parsing the existing bullets. The barrier is not authorship — it is that 34 analyses use 30+ different section-heading conventions and 6 different metadata key spellings, so extraction is 34 bespoke parsers today. Standardising the template retroactively is the single highest-leverage move; it converts ~973 existing claims into structure at near-zero analytic cost. The entry is EXCELLENT by its own standard (a). It is structurally incapable of (b) as it stands, but it is closer to (b) than any layout-family peer, because the clause-level anchor system is already in the prose.
strengths: Quotation fidelity is exact. I brute-force located four DA-04 quotations by scanning all 54 PDF pages: "movement resulting from an actual exercise of a power of sense" -> PDF p.44 (analysis says 44), "never thinks without an image" -> p.47 (says 47), "tool of tools" -> p.48 (says 48), "soul is in a way all existing things" -> p.48 (says 48). Four further quotes verified verbatim against the full extracted text. Eight of eight sampled quotations are correct in both wording and page. This is the strongest verified quotation layer I have seen in the index.

phase05-offset-validation.md is a genuine, empirically derived validation artifact — per-work compression ratios (1.250-2.000 PDF pages per Bekker page) derived from 133 OCR-detected margin landmarks across three zones per major work, with an error column, plus an OCR-characteristics section documenting the asterisk-for-column-letter substitution. Its stated PDF page counts (179/134/120/54/23/9/12/12/10) match pdfinfo EXACTLY. It is the correct answer to the entry's worst defect and it already exists on disk; the fix is to regenerate the JSON layers from it, not to re-derive anything.
phase0-overview.md:307-315 independently records the true PDF end pages per work, so the ground truth for the locator repair is present in TWO files.

Manifest/unit-record agreement is perfect: 34/34 unit_ids match, 0 file-existence gaps in either direction, and 0 field mismatches across label, bekker_range, tier, cluster, two_pass, dissertation_critical, and work. Filename-to-unit_id case mapping is consistent for all 34 (aristotle-meta-05.json <-> META-05) — the 'mixed uppercase unit_id vs lowercase filenames' concern is a deliberate, uniform convention, not drift.

47/47 JSON files parse cleanly. tension-edges.json yields 12/12 edges (this entry is NOT one of the silent-zero schemas), and its CT-01..CT-12 ids are the only namespaced tension ids in compiled-index.json — every other entry uses bare T1..T9, which collide 4-way across the 64-edge array.

entries.verdict: SALVAGEABLE, and worth salvaging — but the JSON layer must be regenerated, not patched. This is the most substantively scholarly entry in the index: 218,142 authored words, 199 Greek-first ontology nodes, 402 evidence-bearing edges, 188 Bekker loci, 164 lemmas, quotations verified exact against the source PDFs, and 2,323 distinct clause-level Bekker addresses already recorded in prose. It also single-handedly supplies 100% of the runtime crossPipelineHooks array via a hardcoded directory literal at compile-corpus-index.py:1239 — a load-bearing dependency nobody declared. Against that, the machine-readable layer is broken in a specific, diagnosable way: the entry ran Phase 0.5, discovered that Bekker-to-PDF mapping is non-linear, wrote the corrected per-work formulas at 15:27:56, regenerated exactly ONE unit record (aristotle-meta-05.json, mtime 15:33:41, and it is the only correct one), and then abandoned the correction — leaving 33 unit records on the superseded linear offset and generating the 188-locus bekker index at 16:23:11 with the same discarded arithmetic. The prose analyses were corrected; the JSON was not; nothing records which layer wins. The result is that the entry's own ground truth sits three files away from the data it contradicts. On top of that, the structured layer is unjoinable to itself: per-source edges use Greek-script node ids and global edges use latin snake_case (only 33 of 245 triples shared), ontology `units` cells emit 35 tokens that are not unit_ids, 63/72 hooks have unresolvable sourceConcepts and 47/72 unroutable targets, and the compiler's global name-dedup merges Aristotelian Truth/Logos/psyche with Heideggerian ones and keeps only the longest definition. Judged against its own cluster template it is excellent-with-broken-locators; judged against claim-and-clause-level it is structurally incapable today but unusually close — the clause addresses exist, they just live in markdown bullets under 30 different heading conventions. Recommended path: (1) regenerate all 34 pdf_pages and all 188 bekker pdf_page values from phase05-offset-validation.md and verify a sample by text match, as I did; (2) promote the prose analyses to the source of truth for locators and delete the linear-offset arithmetic from the pipeline; (3) unify edge node ids on one alphabet and key them to ontology node ids rather than display names; (4) standardise the phase2 template and mint claim ids for the ~844 unIDed Bekker-anchored bullets, which converts existing prose into claim-level structure without new reading; (5) extend the compiler past Section 3A so the 30 authored tensions and the contested-node dossiers stop being invisible. Do not rebuild the scholarship — it is the best in the corpus. Rebuild only the serialization.

The source PDF exists (13,701,366 bytes) and the declared offset book = pdf − 2 was empirically confirmed (pdf 35 carries printed folio 33; pdf 36 carries the Bonsiepe passage cited at p.34). The video-seed directory /mnt/d/PhD/Dissertation/Media/VLE/ exists. The FCM digests and the RODA method files all resolve. entries.granularity_gap: Finest encoded unit: a CLAIM. This is the only entry in the batch that already encodes claim-level structure machine-readably — 139 claim objects across 7 unit JSONs, each {text, locus} (48 also carry an id), plus 143 key_terms with loci, 105 interlocutors, 68 design_principles with loci, and 21 ro_hooks. Distance to the claim-level target is therefore ONE step, not two: the claims exist and are individually page-anchored; what is missing is (a) globally unique IDs (91/139 have none, 20 collide), (b) linkage from claim → node and claim → edge (the 307 edges and the 139 claims share no key), (c) a uniform schema (8 unit JSONs, 8 shapes), and (d) any reader. Distance to CLAUSE level is a full step further: nothing in the entry stores a sentence span, a character offset, or a quote span; the 38 anchor_phrases in dfd-01/dfd-05 are the closest thing and they are bare strings with no offsets. Additional claim-level material is ALREADY present but unstructured in the unit .md analyses (~34,100 words of prose that restate and expand each claim with fuller loci, e.g. dfd-01-...md:114 gives the Bonsiepe claim with the correct quotation and a page range where the JSON gives a single page). Cost implication: for Wendt the claim layer is a harvest-and-rekey job, not an authoring job.
strengths: The 139-claim / 143-term / 105-interlocutor / 68-principle structured payload in units/*.json is the single most valuable asset in this batch and must survive any redesign — it is claim-level analysis with page loci, already machine-readable.

Locus discipline is real and verified: every one of the 307 edge rows carries a non-empty locus, and all 307 satisfy the declared offset book = pdf − 2. The offset itself was empirically confirmed against the PDF (pdf 35 → printed 33; pdf 36 → the cited Bonsiepe passage).
_synthesis/page-offset-verification.md records 4 named anchors with content descriptions — reproducible, auditable, and the model the other two entries lack.

_synthesis/quality-gates-report.md's word-count gate is exactly right: declared dfd-00 3,908 · 01 6,793 · 02 1,019 · 03 4,176 · 04 5,096 · 05 7,244 · 06 3,564 · 07 2,312 matches `wc -w` on all eight files with zero deviation.

Provenance discipline is explicit and enforced in the bridge layer: bme-vle-read.md separates '§§1–4 as observed (factual)' from '§5–6 anticipatory-application', and 'anticipatory-application' is tagged 7× in dfd-rhetorical-ontology-bridge.md. This three-voice separation (Wendt-says / RO-mapping / environment-application) is exactly what a claim-level index needs and should be generalised.

dfd-07-bibliography-notes.json holds 120 sources, each {author,title,year,strand}, zero missing years, zero duplicate (author,title), across 10 named strands — a clean, immediately reusable interlocutor spine.

The BME video seed read is genuinely good empirical work: three Whisper transcripts, curated contact sheets, and a design read that names concrete mechanics (E to engage, Q to close, 3-second buffer, adaptive bitrate, S3 delivery, Hide-POV toggle) rather than gesturing.
Per-source and synthesis edge layers are provably identical here, which makes this entry the correct control case for deciding which layer is authoritative corpus-wide.
entries.verdict: SALVAGEABLE, and the most salvageable entry in the batch — but its self-reporting cannot be trusted and its runtime footprint is a rounding error. Judged against its own standard (the cluster template plus its own quality gates) it is close to exemplary: 8/8 units built to declared depth, word counts exact, 307 edges every one of which carries a verified locus, a 120-source bibliography, a 95-lemma glossary, two payload documents, a video seed case with real provenance discipline. Judged against the claim/clause-level target it is the ONLY entry here that is not structurally incapable of it — 139 page-anchored claims already sit in the unit JSONs, so the claim layer is a harvest, not a rewrite. What must be fixed is not the analysis but the plumbing and the self-description: the tension layer is silently zeroed by a schema mismatch, the manifest and quality-gates report both misdescribe the entry's own registration state and misstate what compiled-index.json contains, the synthesis glossary degrades a quotation the unit layer gets right, the entry certifies a source PDF as 'OCR clean' that is visibly mangled, and the 15 node names that do reach runtime are composite phrases that cannot match prose. Rebuild the interfaces (unit schema, tension schema, claim IDs, node names); preserve the content wholesale.

entries.granularity_gap: Finest STRUCTURED unit: a chapter-pair (14 units, each covering 2 book chapters, 9–17 pages). But the finest AUTHORED unit is already a claim: the 14 phase2 analyses each carry a '## 4. Main Positions / Claims' markdown table with columns Claim | Evidence type | Strength | Page ref — 107 rows in total (f0 6, f1 6, f2 5, f3 9, f4 6, f5 7, f6 7, f7 8, m1 8, m2 6, m3 9, m4 9, m5 9, m6 12). Alongside them sit 180 key-concept rows (Concept | German | Definition | Centrality | First appearance | Related concepts), 67 tension rows, 73 interlocutor rows, 201 German-term rows and 206 machine-readable local edges in fenced JSON. So claim-level material EXISTS and is even column-typed with evidence-type and strength grading — a richer claim schema than Wendt's {text, locus}. It is trapped in markdown tables that nothing parses, and the corresponding uex-*.json 'unit records' are 800-byte scaffolds with none of it. Distance to claim level: one extraction pass over 14 files with a stable table schema (Section 3, 4, 5, 7, 8 are identically headed in all 14 — the most uniform prose layer in the batch). Distance to CLAUSE level: full step further; page refs are page-granular ('pp. 49–50'), there are no sentence spans or character offsets, and quotations appear inline in the Hierarchical Outline bullets without any span record. Cost implication: for Uexküll the claim layer is a parse job over a genuinely regular format, not an authoring job.
strengths: The most internally consistent manifest in the batch: 14/14 unit records match the manifest on filename, label, chapter list, two_pass, dissertation_critical, page_count and offset with zero deviations. Gate W1 is settled by the filesystem, not by argument.

phase0-overview.md's 'PDF Offset Verification' table is the batch's best provenance apparatus — four named anchors with content descriptions, one of which is recorded as FAILING with a hypothesis and a follow-up instruction. Honest negative reporting like this should be mandatory.

The 14 phase2 analyses share an identical 9-section skeleton (Metadata, Hierarchical Outline, Key Concepts, Main Positions/Claims, Interlocutors, Cross-Pipeline References, Tensions, German Terms, Graph Edges). This regularity is what makes a claim-level harvest cheap here and expensive in Rickert.

The '## 4. Main Positions / Claims' table schema — Claim | Evidence type | Strength | Page ref — is a better claim model than anything else in the batch: it records not just the claim and its page but the KIND of warrant and the analyst's confidence. 107 rows of it.

contested-nodes.md (19,815 chars) maps six concepts that shift meaning across the book, each with 'The Shift', a core-ambiguity discussion, and an explicit 'Translation Dispute' section. This is exactly the 'every weakness' layer the ultimate goal asks for, already written.

Quotation fidelity in the prose layer is genuinely good where I could check it: 'All animal subjects, from the simplest to the most complex, are inserted into their environments to the same degree of perfection' (cited p.50) is verbatim on pdf 54 = book 50; 'The effect mark extinguishes the perception mark' (cited p.49) is verbatim on pdf 53 = book 49.

global-edges.csv and the phase2 files use CORRECT German orthography (Gegengefüge, Planmäßigkeit, Bedeutungsträger, Außenfront) — a correct lemma set exists in the entry and can be used to repair the corrupted layers.

Edge relations are controlled: 11 values across 152 rows (depends_on 46, contrasts_with 23, presupposes 20, refines 20, operationalizes 18, explains 14, is_meaning_of 3, undermines 3, supports 2, historicizes 2, exemplifies 1) with 6 edge_domain values. Compare Rickert's 189.
entries.verdict: SALVAGEABLE with a mandatory normalisation pass — the analysis is strong, the plumbing between layers is broken by an orthography problem that must be fixed before anything else. Against its own standard it does well: the manifest is exact, the offset is verified with a disclosed failure, the 14 analyses are uniform and dense (34,210 words), the edge relation vocabulary is controlled, and spot-checked quotations are verbatim. Against the claim/clause-level target it is not structurally incapable — 107 claim rows with evidence-type and strength grading already exist, in a regular table format, across 14 identically-shaped files. But four things must change before either standard can be met: (1) the German lemma key must be normalised to one orthography — the correct one already exists in global-edges.csv and the phase2 files, while book-level-ontology.md and uex-german-appendix.md (the ones that reach runtime) publish umlaut-stripped forms; (2) node names must stop carrying English parentheticals, which currently makes all 34 German canonical terms unmatchable; (3) the appendix must be reconciled — 100 claimed, 91 in .md, 148 in .json, with 44 dangling node links; (4) the 206-vs-152 edge divergence needs an authority decision. The uex-structured/*.json 'unit records' should be treated as what they are, pagination scaffolds, and either filled from the .md tables or dropped. Do not rebuild the analysis; rebuild the join keys.

entries.granularity_gap: Finest STRUCTURED unit: a chapter section (65 sections, each a heading + page range + tag list) — nominally the finest structural granularity in the batch, but each section record carries zero analytic content, so the finest CONTENTFUL structured unit is the chapter. Claim-level material exists but is markedly less structured than in Wendt or Uexküll: '## 4. Main Positions' is PROSE with bolded or ### position headers, yielding 75 identifiable discrete positions across the 10 files (ch1 8, ch2 6, ch3 8, ch4 5, ch5 10, ch6 8, ch7 7, ch8 7, conclusion 8, intro 8) and zero table rows anywhere — versus Uexküll's 107 typed claim rows and Wendt's 139 JSON claim objects. '## 5. Tensions and Open Questions' contributes a further 51 discrete tensions (5 per chapter, 6 in the conclusion). The genuinely machine-readable fine-grained layer is the 242 local edges in fenced JSON, but 8 schemas and 189 relation values make them unusable without normalisation, and 120 of them carry no locus field at all. Concept tables give 146 rows. Distance to claim level: TWO steps here, not one — extraction from prose (harder than parsing a table) plus schema unification across 10 divergent file shapes. Distance to clause level: unreached; no spans, no offsets, and the page loci that do exist inherit the wrong pdf offset. Cost implication: Rickert is the most expensive of the three to lift to claim level despite having the most words (43,644).
strengths: The prose analyses are the deepest in the batch by volume — 43,644 words over 10 chapters, with phase2-introduction.md at 6,301 words and phase2-ch1.md at 5,491 — and the concept definitions that reach runtime are substantial (414–619 chars each, with embedded page-anchored quotations).

rickert-structured/manifest.json is internally exact: all 10 chapter_ids, files, titles, pages, pdf_pages, section_count and part values match their chapter JSONs, and total_sections 65 equals the actual sum. Section IDs are systematic and collision-free (ch1-s1..ch8-s7, conc-s1..s7, intro-s1..s8; 0 duplicates).

tension-edges.json uses the fully-supported schema — node_a/node_b plus dependency_edge{relation,note} and conflict_edge{relation,note} plus synthesis and chapters — and is the only tension file in the batch that reaches runtime with the dependency/conflict distinction INTACT (unlike Uexküll, where they collapse, and Wendt, where they vanish). This is the schema the other entries should adopt.

The §3D 'Contested/Unstable Nodes' table is exactly the 'every weakness' layer the ultimate goal calls for: 6 concepts (Chora, Kairos, Invention, Networks, Dwelling, Attunement) each with chapters, a prose account of how the concept shifts, and an explicit Resolution column that sometimes declines to resolve ('The uncanny/haunted dimension of Ch3 is never fully reconciled with the constructive dwelling of Ch7-8').

The 242 local edges, whatever their schema chaos, represent per-chapter relational analysis at ~24 edges per chapter with notes — four times the density of the published synthesis layer. The content is worth rescuing even though the encoding is not.
Book-page citations verify: the Chora node's quotation cited '(Ch1, 55)' is on printed page 55, and the quoted text is verbatim to its truncation point.

65 section records with heading + page range give a real subdivision of the book below chapter level — the structural skeleton for a claim-level index already exists here, it just has nothing hanging off it.
entries.verdict: REBUILD the plumbing; keep the prose. This is the weakest of the three by construction quality and the most consequential by what it exposes. Against its own standard it is thin: no quality-gates report, no manifest for the analysis half, no offset verification, three unreconciled concept inventories (15 / 25 / 33), and a synthesis edge layer that shares not one triple with the 242 edges its own chapters authored. Against the claim/clause-level target it is the furthest of the three: its 75 positions and 51 tensions live in prose rather than tables, its 65 section records are empty shells, and its finest machine-readable layer — the local edges — is spread across 8 schemas with 189 relation values, one file using whole sentences as relations and another using ALL-CAPS. Two defects are corpus-level rather than entry-level and must be fixed in the compiler regardless of what happens to this entry: the _parse_header_section field-continuation bug that dumped 10,009 characters of §3B/3C/3D/3G into one node's centralityTier and 973 garbage tokens into its units (any entry with content after its last §3A node is corrupted the same way), and the name-keyed deduplication that let Boredom Secondary overwrite Rickert's Kairos tier and type. The pdf_page_offset error is entry-level but critical: every pdf locus in the entry is wrong by 2–5 pages and the drift is monotonic, so a single constant cannot fix it — the entry needs a per-chapter anchor table of the kind Wendt and Uexküll already have. The 43,644 words of analysis and the 6-node contested-nodes table are genuinely valuable and must survive; almost everything between them and runtime should be re-authored.

PRIOR-CLAIM VERDICTS (tested against this batch only)

1. "~310 unit records, 691 unit analyses, ~9,762 distinct edges on disk; ZERO reach runtime." — PARTIAL / mostly CONFIRMED. Batch contributes 32 unit records (Wendt 8, Uexküll 14, Rickert 10) and 32 unit analyses. Edge rows on disk in this batch: 307 per-source + 307 synthesis (Wendt) + 152 (Uexküll) + 56 (Rickert) = 822 CSV rows, PLUS 206 Uexküll and 242 Rickert edges embedded in fenced JSON inside the phase2 markdown (448 more, which a filesystem-level CSV census would miss entirely), PLUS 190 Mermaid arrow-edges. ZERO edge rows and ZERO unit records/analyses reach runtime — CONFIRMED. But "ZERO reach runtime" is wrong as a blanket statement about these entries: 75 ontology nodes (Wendt 15, Uexküll 35, Rickert 25) and 17 tension edges (Uexküll 10, Rickert 7) DO reach compiled-index.json. Reachability by bytes: Wendt ~0.9%, Uexküll ~4.4%, Rickert ~7.5% (nominally 10% but ~10 KB is garbage).

2. "The compiler reads only 4 filename patterns … plus tension-edges.json." — CONFIRMED with a correction: there are FIVE ontology patterns. collect_ontology_nodes() (compile-corpus-index.py:1180-1247) tries `book-level-ontology.md` and falls back to `cluster-ontology.md` for header-format entries; `*-ontology.md` and `*-cross-pipeline-hooks.md` are Aristotle-only (the latter hard-coded to `CORPUS_INDEX / "Aristotle - Complete Works"`). All three of my entries ARE in TEXT_DIRS (lines 92-100 for Rickert/Uexküll, 128-132 for Wendt), so the failure mode here is not registration — it is that registration buys you one markdown file and one JSON file per entry.

3. "42 header dialects, 633 relation values, 31 unenforced ID prefixes." — PLAUSIBLE, and this batch alone supplies a large share. CSV header dialects here: 4 (Wendt per-unit `source,relation,target,locus,note`; Wendt global `unit,source,relation,target,locus,note`; Uexküll `source,target,relation,edge_domain,units,note`; Rickert `source,relation,edge_domain,target,note,chapters` — note Uexküll and Rickert have overlapping field SETS in different ORDERS). Relation values: 12 (Wendt) + 11 (Uexküll) + 9 (Rickert CSV) but 189 more in Rickert's in-markdown local edges, so ~200 distinct from three entries. ID prefixes: dfd- (Wendt units), bare C1..CN (Wendt claims, colliding), U-F0..U-M6 (Uexküll), T1..T12 (all three tension files, colliding across entries), ch1-s1/conc-s1/intro-s1 (Rickert sections).

4. "Only ~10 manifests record source PDFs; 9 entries have NO machine-readable source path." — REFUTED for this batch. All three have a machine-readable source path (manifest.json:7 sourcePdf / manifest.json:3 source_pdf / manifest.json:6 pdf_path) and all three resolve on disk (13.7 MB, 197.2 MB, 38.7 MB). Zero broken paths across ~12 declared cross-references I stat'd, including the RODA method files, the FCM king-salvo digests, and the /mnt/d video seed directory.

5. "Only 2 of 27 entries have a quality-gates-report.md; only 1 has machine-readable metrics." — CONSISTENT. Wendt has one (markdown table, human-readable only); Uexküll and Rickert have none. BRIEF-SPECIFIC ANSWERS

Wendt: 48 files CONFIRMED. 8 units dfd-00..dfd-07 CONFIRMED (the prior undercount of 7 is refuted; all 8 have a .json, a .md and an -edges.csv). 614 edge rows CONFIRMED as 307 + 307. Uexküll: 47 files CONFIRMED. GATE W1 SETTLED AT 14, and not by argument — by the filesystem. 14 uex-*.json unit records, 14 phase2-uex-*.md analyses, 14 unit entries in the manifest, `total_units: 14`, 14 unit columns in concept-matrix.csv (U-F0..U-F7, U-M1..U-M6), and 14 distinct unit tokens in global-edges.csv. The "15" almost certainly came from counting manifest.json as a fifteenth file in uex-structured/. Note the entry's edge row count is 152 in the synthesis file but 206 in the per-unit layer.

Rickert: 32 files CONFIRMED, 10 units CONFIRMED, 56 edge rows CONFIRMED. THE POLLUTED NODE IS FOUND. It is `ontologyNodes[446]`, name `Preparatory Rhetoric`, text `Rickert - Ambient Rhetoric`. Its `centralityTier` is 10,009 characters and its `units` array is 973 tokens — I confirmed both lengths exactly. What got absorbed, precisely: the node is §3A's LAST node (book-level-ontology.md:184), and parse_header_ontology splits on `^\*\*\d+\.\s+`, so its section runs to EOF. Its last bullet, `- **Centrality**: peripheral` (line 189), opens a field that nothing closes, because in _parse_header_section the continuation branch `elif current_key and stripped:` is evaluated BEFORE the terminator branch `elif stripped.startswith("###") or stripped.startswith("---"): break` — the break is unreachable while a key is open. Centrality therefore swallows lines 191–258: the `---` rule, the `## 3B: Global Edge List` heading, the entire 56-row markdown edge table, the `## 3C: Tension Layer` heading and `### Tension 1: Withdrawal vs. Disclosure`. It stops at line 259 only because `- **Node A**: Withdrawal` matches the bold-field regex and opens a new key. Fields then cycle through the seven tensions' Node A / Node B / Dependency edge / Conflict edge / Synthesis / Chapters bullets, each overwriting the last; the FINAL `- **Chapters**: Ch6, Ch7, Ch8` (Tension 7, line 312) then swallows lines 314–337 — the `## 3D: Contested/Unstable Nodes` heading, its 6-row table, the `## 3G: Macro-Trajectory` heading and all three paragraphs of the macro-trajectory essay. parse_units() shreds that on whitespace into the 973 tokens, which is why units begins ['Ch6','Ch7','Ch8','---','##','3D:','Contested/Unstable','Nodes','|','Node',...]. The same bug fires twice more in milder form at the §3A tier boundaries: 'Thing / Gathering' has centralityTier 'core ### important nodes' and 'Technics / Technology' has 'important ### peripheral nodes'. This is a compiler defect, not a Rickert defect — any entry with content after its last §3A node is corrupted identically.

CROSS-ENTRY OBSERVATIONS

The single most important finding for the redesign is that claim-level material is ALREADY AUTHORED in all three entries, in three different containers of decreasing tractability: Wendt has 139 claim objects with page loci in unit JSON (parse and rekey); Uexküll has 107 claim rows in uniform markdown tables typed by evidence-kind and strength, across 14 identically-headed files (parse); Rickert has 75 positions in prose across 10 divergently-headed files (extract). Add 206 + 242 machine-readable local edges hidden in fenced JSON inside markdown that no CSV-level census will ever see. The claim layer is not a greenfield authoring programme — for two of three entries it is an extraction problem.

Three things surprised me. First, quotation fidelity is BETTER in the unit/prose layer than in the synthesis layer: Wendt's unit .md and edge CSV both give Bonsiepe's "the tissue of the relations" correctly at (p.34 / pdf 36), while the _synthesis terminology appendix drops the article and misplaces the page; Rickert's CSV strips the quotation marks its own §3B table preserves. Synthesis is where fidelity is lost. Second, three entries in one batch have three different page-offset regimes and only one is correct-and-verified: Wendt declares book = pdf − 2 with four anchors and it holds on all 307 loci and against the PDF; Uexküll declares +4 with four anchors, one of which is recorded as FAILING, and +4 holds everywhere I tested; Rickert declares a constant 20 with no anchors at all and the true offset is 18/16/15 depending where you are in the book. The entry with no verification apparatus is the entry that is wrong. Third, the German orthography problem in Uexküll is worse than a normalisation nuisance — the entry contains a CORRECT lemma set (global-edges.csv, phase0-overview.md, all 14 phase2 files use Planmäßigkeit, Gegengefüge, Bedeutungsträger) and a CORRUPTED one (book-level-ontology.md and uex-german-appendix.md strip umlauts; tension-edges.json and concept-matrix.csv use ae/ue digraphs), and it is precisely the corrupted files that the compiler reads. The repair material is already in the repository.

One systemic reachability point worth separating from the count arguments: of the 75 node names that DO reach runtime from this batch, 51 contain a slash, semicolon, parenthetical or ' + ' — 34/35 Uexküll names carry an English gloss in parentheses, 10/15 Wendt names are whole clauses. build_canonical_terms() sorts these by length descending "for greedy matching" against running prose. 'Gegengefuge (counterstructure)' is a canonical term; 'Gegengefüge' is not. So even the reachable fraction is substantially unmatchable, which means the effective runtime yield of these three entries is lower than the 0.9% / 4.4% / 7.5% byte figures suggest.

Finally, no ligature corruption (benefcial-class pdfium damage) and no mojibake were found anywhere in the three entries. But the Wendt SOURCE PDF is badly OCR-damaged ("\Y./e", "thts", "strategics", "rnkmg", "lvITT", "prope,1r") despite phase0-overview.md:25 certifying "PDF OCR clean" — a different corruption vector than the known pdfium bug, and one that no existing check would catch.

entries.granularity_gap:
FINEST UNIT ACTUALLY ENCODED: the article, decomposed one level down into (a) 233 `sections` records (title + summary + page, avg 6.9/unit) and (b) 233 `readings` records shaped {claim, type, stance, locus, tag} (avg 6.9/unit). The `readings` array IS a claim-level slot -- it is the only place in the entry where a proposition is a first-class addressable object with a page and a provenance tag. It is roughly ONE level below the article and ONE level above nothing: at ~7 claims per 20-page article it captures the thesis-bearing claims and discards everything else.

DISTANCE TO THE TARGET. Claim-level: the slot exists but the density is off by roughly an order of magnitude. Clause-level: entirely absent -- there is no sentence id, no character offset, no bbox, no quotation span object anywhere in the entry. Loci are page numbers and page RANGES ('p.461-465', 'p.15-16, 24-25'), never sub-page anchors, so even the claims that ARE structured cannot be resolved to a sentence in the source.

CRITICALLY: a large body of claim-level material IS already present, unstructured, inside the prose analyses, and this materially lowers the cost of the programme. Quantified over the 34 unit .md files (529,053 bytes, each with an identical 7-section skeleton):
  - 1,471 page-locus mentions of the form p.NN / pp.NN
  - 522 (FE...) tags = the source's own published claim
  - 548 FAITHFUL-<author> tags = close paraphrase of a specific passage
  - 207 (P/anticipatory-application) tags = our interpretive link
  - 394 quoted spans of >=25 characters
That is ~1,277 provenance-tagged assertions in prose against 233 in JSON: roughly 5.5x more claim-level content already written than is currently structured, and each prose assertion already carries the two fields the structured record needs (a locus and a provenance tag). The extraction problem is therefore closer to a parsing job than an authoring job. Each unit .md also carries a section-6 'Concordance feed' markdown table (construct row | media-condition column | locus | note) -- e.g. 14 rows in ped-sec-06 -- which is already a per-claim tuple in table form.

WHAT WOULD HAVE TO BE ADDED: (1) a sentence/clause id scheme with character offsets into a canonical extracted text (none exists; extraction metadata is only {tool: pdftotext, date, ocr_confidence}); (2) sub-page loci -- the corpus already has a bbox/verbatim capability elsewhere (WRAITH/Marker), and 33 of 34 units are pdftotext-clean per the manifest's own OCR audit, so this is feasible; (3) promotion of the 1,277 prose assertions into readings-shaped records; (4) a stable schema for readings (currently 3 item shapes with type/stance contamination in 11 items and 5 bare strings); (5) a quotation-span object -- the 394 quoted spans currently have no identity and no per-quote page, since a single paragraph-terminal (FAITHFUL-X, p.461-465) tag frequently covers 4+ distinct verbatim quotations, which is exactly how the ped-sec-29 'sense of being in the place' fabrication survived.

STRUCTURAL VERDICT ON (a) vs (b): the entry is excellent by its own cluster-template standard -- 34/34 units complete, 0 stubs (smallest unit JSON is 6,756 bytes), 0 dangling ped-sec ids anywhere in 127 files, concept-matrix perfectly consistent with the ontology, anchor-pointers table perfectly consistent with the edges. But it is STRUCTURALLY INCAPABLE of the claim/clause-level target as built, for three reasons that no amount of care at this layer fixes: the locus vocabulary bottoms out at the page range; there is no id space below ped-sec-NN (the 60 ontology nodes and 10 DA-NN axes are the only other identifiers, and 40/40 debate edges do not even use the DA ids); and the one channel that reaches runtime carries 60 concept nodes and nothing else -- no claim, no reading, no edge, no quotation has any runtime existence at all.
strengths: Referential integrity is essentially perfect at the unit level. A scan of all 127 files for `ped-sec-\\d+` found ZERO ids outside ped-sec-01..34 -- no dangling unit references in any md, json, csv or mmd. All 34 manifest folders exist, all 34 sourceFile paths resolve, all 34 file triples are present, and 0 edge rows have a source column disagreeing with their own filename.

concept-matrix.csv is bit-exact against cluster-ontology: for all 34 columns the set of units marked 'x' equals the node's `units` array exactly (0 of 34 mismatches). This is the cleanest cross-artifact consistency I found anywhere in the entry and should be the model for the rest.

cluster-ontology.md and cluster-ontology.json are perfectly synchronized: 60 nodes each, zero name differences in either direction, zero units-list differences across all 60 nodes. The JSON is clean, flat and immediately ingestible -- it is the fix for the CRITICAL canonicalTerms defect, already written.

bridge-sources/anchor-pointers.md's 34-row table validates 100% against the per-unit edge files: for every unit, the declared VLE anchor set and the declared bridges-to-part-iii count match the CSVs exactly (0 problems across 34 rows). It also correctly declares itself derived rather than hand-transcribed.

The provenance tagging discipline is genuinely rigorous and consistently applied: FE (source's own claim) / FAITHFUL-<author> (close paraphrase of a specific passage) / P-anticipatory-application (our interpretive link, never the source's). 1,277 tagged assertions across the 34 analyses. Crucially the P tag is used honestly against the authors' own interest -- e.g. ped-sec-34's bridge edge says the VLE F7 finding 'is a stronger empirical hit for the general presence/co-viewing theme than for any construct this review develops in depth ... since this review never operationalizes social presence itself'.

The entry documents a NEGATIVE finding as its headline result and does not paper over it: cluster-ontology.md sections 1 and 5 establish that the CMC-to-VR social-presence bridge the plan anticipated 'mostly does not exist in the literature itself', verified by full-text checks that ped-sec-33 and ped-sec-34 cite none of the CMC canon. citation-network.json's keyFinding records the same at the citation level. This is the kind of result an index is uniquely able to produce and a redesign must preserve.

manifest.json is the most substantive manifest in the corpus: 16 top-level keys including a 5-entry planCorrections log (author-name discrepancy, a wrong steering-note prediction, the post-Phase-1 extension, a MISLABELED PDF caught by pdfinfo before any content was built under a false attribution, and a Phase-2 finding that a unit does not perform the role the plan assigned it), an ocrAudit with per-source word counts and a named OCR-LOW unit, an excluded[] record with reason, themes, debate_axes_seeds, and crossPipelineTargets with real paths.

The unit markdown analyses are uniform and dense: all 34 have exactly 7 top-level sections, none is a stub (smallest 6,897 bytes, largest 21,436), and each carries a section-6 'Concordance feed' table of construct x media-condition x locus x note tuples. This uniformity is what makes the 1,277 prose assertions mechanically harvestable.

The readings array, where it holds its canonical shape (225 of 233 items), is exactly the right object for the claim-level programme: {claim, type: READING/CLAIM, stance, locus, tag}. 228 of 233 carry a locus. Any redesign should keep this shape verbatim and extend it downward, not replace it.

The entry knows and records its own bridge semantics honestly: 24 speculative grounds-measure edges to the Boredom dataset were RETIRED in a documented 2026-07-16 rescope on the grounds that 'they were backwards', with the rationale written into manifest.json, anchor-pointers.md, the ontology summary and the .mmd. Retiring edges for being conceptually wrong is rarer and more valuable than adding them.
entries.verdict: SALVAGEABLE, and worth salvaging -- but the registration layer must be rebuilt, not patched. On its own stated standard this is one of the strongest entries in the corpus: 34/34 units complete with zero stubs, zero dangling ids across 127 files, all 41 JSONs parsing, 34/34 source PDFs resolvable from a machine-readable manifest, a concept matrix that is bit-exact against its ontology, an anchor-pointer table that validates 100% against the edge layer, an honest negative headline finding, and a documented mislabeled-PDF catch that prevented a fabricated attribution. That authoring quality must be preserved. But the entry's relationship to runtime is close to a total loss and is actively harmful: ~1.1% of authored bytes reach compiled-index.json, and the 1.1% that does arrives CORRUPTED -- 19 of 60 node names are truncated and their parentheticals ('technological', 'control', '1976', 'HMD', 'Pitfall 1') are injected into the global canonicalTerms greedy matcher as if they were Greek lemmas. A clean cluster-ontology.json sits on disk, unread, containing the correct names. That single adapter is the highest-value fix available and it is a compiler change, not an entry change. The entry is correctly registered in TEXT_DIRS (compile-corpus-index.py:115-119) and does contribute 44 ontologyNodes, so this is a schema mismatch, not an unregistered entry. The compiler reports success and cannot do otherwise: main() prints one aggregate tension count plus a per-text breakdown of NODES only, so no per-entry zero is observable. Consequence: the entry's volume-level synthesis — which the file's own header at line 10 self-declares as `dissertation_load_bearing_count: 8` (a header count; no individual tension carries a `dissertation_load_bearing` field, and the `notes` array names only T-001–T-005) and every one of whose 12 tensions carries a non-empty `dissertation_implication` — never reaches the live consumer at src/god-agent/universal/corpus-index-provider.ts:147, which is the sole path by which tensions enter drafting prompts. Separately, against the claim-level target: these tensions are volume-scoped (supporting_units name whole chapters; page_anchors give ranges like "167-180"), two granularity levels above clause-level, and the runtime edge schema has no slot for page_anchors, dissertation_implication, or type — so a naive fix would recover the edges while discarding the fields that make them usable.

entries.granularity_gap: Finest unit actually encoded = the ARTICLE, with a per-article inventory beneath it. There is no ID for anything below the article: concepts, readings, game_elements, themes, interlocutors and tensions are all label-only objects or bare strings. The edge layer is strictly article→label (all 12 files are stars from the unit id), so no claim participates in a relation. Distance to claim level: two full levels — you would need (1) stable IDs for each of the 1,043 sub-unit objects, and (2) edges whose SOURCE is one of those IDs rather than the unit. Distance to clause level: three levels — there is no locus anchoring below the section (`readings[].locus` is 'General Introduction (pp.6-7); Part 1 sec.1 (p.8)', i.e. section+page, never a line or sentence). CRITICALLY, claim-level material IS already present but unstructured: the 86 `readings` objects each carry a one-sentence claim plus a page locus, the 56 `tensions` are stated as claim-pairs ('Procedural rhetoric vs. player freedom: the honor system is framed as valorizing the possibility of choice, yet Bagnoli concedes that free will is itself biased...'), and the 38 `debate_axis_positions` are per-unit stances. That is roughly 180 claim-shaped objects already authored across 12 units, plus 31,501 words of unit prose containing many more. Promoting the existing readings/tensions/debate_axis_positions to first-class ID'd claim nodes is a re-keying job, not a re-reading job — which materially lowers the cost of the programme for this entry.
strengths: The per-unit/synthesis edge layers agree EXACTLY: 68+27+32+12+42+58+35+53+38+58+39+44 = 506 = global-edges.csv row count, with identical relation histograms on both sides. This is the only entry in the batch with a lossless synthesis layer.

A controlled, small relation vocabulary: 12 relations only (treats-game-element 144, cites 143, defines 68, instances-in-text 29, extends 24, shifts-debate-axis 22, concedes 19, qualifies 18, contests-reading-of 11, contests 10, extends-reading-of 10, cites-cluster-author 8). The edge CSV header `source,relation,target,locus,note` is EXACTLY the schema the cluster template mandates — RDR2 is the only entry in the batch that conforms.

An honest, self-critical quality-gates report that reports a failed gate (intra-cluster citations 4 vs 10) as a substantive finding about a pre-paradigmatic field rather than hiding it, and that correctly documents how compiled-index.json is actually built.
Verbatim discipline is genuinely clean: 823 quoted spans in the unit .md files, longest is 19 words — the declared '<25-word' policy holds with margin. Zero pdfium ligature corruption, zero mojibake.

The game-element concordance (159 game_elements across 12 units, with mechanics/missions/regions facets and three named RODA anchors) is a genuinely novel cross-cutting axis with no analogue elsewhere in the corpus.

entries.verdict: SALVAGEABLE, and the cheapest of the four to fix — but only after two structural changes, not one. The entry is excellent by its own stated standard on everything the template can count: 12/12 unit trios, 506 lossless edges against a floor of 144, 10 debates, 10 contested readings, 65 lemmas, 5 graphs, clean verbatim, a controlled 12-relation vocabulary, and the only conforming edge header in the batch. It is nonetheless 0% reachable, and — the finding that matters most — the fix its own quality-gates report proposes (add a TEXT_DIRS entry) would be a silent no-op, because I ran the compiler's own parse_header_ontology and parse_table_ontology against cluster-ontology.md and both return zero nodes. The ontology must first be rewritten into the `#### N. Name` + `- **key**: value` header format that the registered Boredom Secondary entry uses. Against the claim/clause target the entry is structurally incapable as built: it has no identifier for anything below the article, and its entire edge layer is a star from the unit, so no claim can ever be an endpoint. That said, ~180 claim-shaped objects (86 readings, 56 tensions, 38 debate-axis positions) are already authored and only need IDs — so a redesign should re-key rather than re-read. Preserve the concordance, the relation vocabulary, the lossless per-unit↔global correspondence, and the honest gate reporting; discard the label-only concept joins and the '# dfd…' titles.

provenance.notes: ZERO declared source paths — the worst provenance in the batch alongside Motion and Time. There is no manifest.json, and grep -rn '\.pdf' over all 46 files returns nothing.
