So the entry knows exactly which page of which printed article every claim sits on — it simply never records which file on disk that article is. Every one of the 288 canonical loci and 708 edge page-anchors is therefore unverifiable without a human re-identifying the PDFs.

entries.granularity_gap: Finest unit actually encoded = the SECTION and, for one unit, the CONCEPT. The unit records reach two sub-levels below the article: `section_structure` (51 objects, each with section_id, heading, pdf_pages, book_pages, summary) and `outline` (181 objects at paragraph-cluster granularity, e.g. phx-04-caston.json outline[5]: 'Cluster 6 (PDF 6, book 26, §II cont.): Caston distinguishes (1) thinking consists in the SAME KIND of process as perceiving, and (1\') thinking does not differ from perceiving in any way at all. Theophrastus\' formula ἢ ταὐτὸν ἢ παραπαλήσιον…'). Distance to claim level is ONE level, not two — and for the Aristotle axis it is effectively ZERO: phx-aristotle-loci-concordance.json holds 288 canonical Bekker loci resolved to page+column with 463 per-unit theme annotations attached, which is clause-granular on the primary-text side. Crucially, ONE UNIT ALREADY DOES CLAIM-LEVEL EDGES: phx-03-frede-edges.csv is the only per-unit file in the batch whose sources are concept IDs rather than the unit — 18 distinct sources including PHX-03-FREDE:C10, :C11, :R1, :R2, :T1, :T3. The other seven files are stars from the unit. So the format demonstrably CAN carry claim-level structure and one unit proves it; the gap is uniformity, not capability. Already-present unstructured claim material: 66 `readings` objects each with a full thesis statement plus key_anchors (phx-04-caston readings[1] states the causal-powers thesis in 60 words with three Bekker anchors and a subjunctive formalisation), 46 `tensions` each stated as a claim-pair with Bekker citations, 235 `concepts` with glosses, and 181 outline clusters — roughly 528 claim-shaped objects already authored, plus 66k words of unit prose and 28k of synthesis prose. Reaching clause level would additionally require sentence-offset anchoring, which nothing in the entry has.
strengths: _synthesis/render-validation.txt is the only machine-checkable quality artefact in the batch that VERIFIES: it claims citation-network 35 edges, concept-debate 22, discipline-cluster 22, aristotle-locus-density 38, cross-pipeline-bridge 16 — I counted the .mmd edge lines and all five match exactly. It also records the tool version (mmdc v11.14.0) and date.

entries.verdict: SOUND IN SUBSTANCE, BROKEN IN PLUMBING — preserve the content, rebuild the interface. This is the most valuable entry in the batch by a wide margin: 2,505 structured sub-unit objects, a 288-locus Bekker concordance with 463 theme annotations, 213 canonicalised Greek lemmas, a 41-node ontology with contiguous IDs and defended merge logic, and the only render-validation artefact in the corpus whose numbers I could verify exactly against the files. It is also the entry the whole cluster programme was modelled on — RDR2's manifest names it as its 'model' and the 2026-07-15 template names it as a precedent. Yet it reaches runtime at 0%, it is the only entry in the batch with NO manifest.json, it declares NO source path for any of its eight PDFs, its concept matrix (CM01–CM38) shares not one identifier with its ontology (PHX-C-001–041), its per-unit and synthesis edge layers use incompatible target vocabularies so the two cannot be reconciled by string match, and it silently drops two Papachristou edges (phx-08-papachristou-edges.csv:25 and :57) with nothing recording the loss. Add the verbatim exposure — 49 spans of 25+ words including a 140-word Aquinas/Kocourek block and 66-word blocks of Hawhee's and Nussbaum's own prose — and the entry fails its own cluster template on the verbatim gate, the 3A-parseable gate and the compiler gate simultaneously. Against the claim/clause target it is the CLOSEST of the four: only one level short on the secondary side, already at clause level on the Aristotle side, and phx-03-frede-edges.csv already demonstrates concept-level edges. Do not rebuild the analysis. Rebuild: a manifest with source paths and a verbatim policy, one ID namespace shared by ontology/matrix/edges, a header-format 3A node list, and the Frede edge pattern applied to the other seven units.

entries.granularity_gap: Finest unit actually encoded = the CHAPTER/SECTION, with claim-shaped objects beneath it that lack identity. `outline` holds 44 objects keyed by page range ('Introduction (1-7)', summary 80 words); `concepts` holds 99 objects {id, label, tier, gloss}; `readings` 45 objects each a full thesis; `aristotle_loci` 168 objects {work, bekker, role} where `role` is already a claim ('THE definition of the passions: states on account of which we change/differ pros tas kriseis, accompanied by pain and pleasure'); `tensions` 27 objects typed against dissertation questions ({'id':'TN1','type':'dissertation-T1-2','desc':'Dow is the ALLY: passions involve the subject\'s affirming their content…'}). Distance to clause level: two levels — Bekker line-pairs are recorded on the Aristotle side (168 loci), but no sentence or clause offset exists on the secondary side. Notably, this entry has the FINEST-GRAINED EDGE LAYER of the four: unlike RDR2 and 7 of 8 Phantasia units, all five AES edge files use concept-level or term-level sources (99 distinct sources in global-edges.csv, e.g. 'affirmation as yes-saying', 'appetite-akrasia', "Odysseus's anger (thumos-akrasia)", "'last protasis'"). The edges ARE claim-to-claim. They are unusable only because the endpoints are free-text labels rather than IDs — which makes this the cheapest entry in the batch to lift to claim level: assign IDs to the existing 99 sources and the graph is already there.

entries.verdict: SALVAGEABLE, AND THE CHEAPEST LIFT TO CLAIM LEVEL — but its status metadata must be rebuilt first because it actively lies. The scholarship is strong: five well-chosen units organised around a real debate axis, the only complete per-unit PDF provenance in the batch, an auditable manifest that states expected loci and Greek terms in advance, and — the finding that most changes the redesign calculus — an edge layer that is ALREADY claim-to-claim in all five units, with 99 distinct concept/term-level sources rather than a star from the article. The blockers are identity and honesty, not analysis. On identity: 20 of 26 concept IDs collide (C1 names five different concepts), three incompatible unit-naming schemes coexist (aes-01..05 vs F/K/MA/MG/D vs Fortenbaugh/Konstan/Moss-Akrasia/Moss-ApparentGood/Dow), the ontology and matrix agree on only 23 of ~40 labels, and the concept count is stated three ways (40/38/37). On honesty: manifest phase_status still reports the deep-unit and synthesis phases as 'pending' when both shipped, which would cause any orchestrator to overwrite finished work; global-edges.csv has no unit column and its contributor field fuses Moss 2009 with Moss 2012, destroying attribution for 80 of 210 edges; and the raw loci dump was persisted to /tmp and is gone. Add five verbatim spans that break the entry's own declared 25-word filter (52 words of Konstan's own prose) and it fails its stated standard on content discipline too. entries.granularity_gap: Finest unit actually encoded = the SECTION, and this is the only entry in the batch whose EDGE ENDPOINTS ARE PROPERLY TYPED AND ID'D. amt-01-bowin-edges.csv carries edge_id, contributor, source_type, source_id, relation, target_type, target_id, target_label, evidence_locus, strength, note — 11 columns, and all 58 source_ids resolve to declared objects (C01..C21, R01..R05, L01..L67, G01..G32, T01..T06, plus the unit). 67 aristotle_loci are recorded at Bekker line-pair precision with per-locus roles ('Phys. 4.10.218a8-21 — Puzzle of the ceasing instant; Bowin §3, referenced as temporal-passage metaphysics, not perception of time passing'), which is clause-granular on the primary-text side. Distance to claim level on the secondary side is ONE level: 21 concepts and 5 readings carry summaries that ARE claims ('Perceiving time and grasping time intellectually are distinct modes of cognition; perceiving time does NOT presuppose grasping time intellectually'), and 6 tensions are stated as claim-pairs — roughly 32 claim-shaped objects with STABLE IDs, which no other entry in the batch achieves. Distance to clause level: one further level; no sentence offsets exist. The striking finding is that the entry the brief calls 'abandoned mid-creation' is in fact the ONLY one in the batch whose edge layer is already claim-addressable end to end. What it lacks is scale (1 unit, 58 edges) and any cluster layer — and, fatally, an ontology file. If a redesign wants a schema exemplar, this is it: 37 of 58 edges are still UNIT-sourced, but 21 are already CONCEPT/LOCUS/TENSION/GREEK-TERM-sourced with resolvable IDs.
strengths: The best edge schema in the batch by a distance: edge_id, contributor, source_type, source_id, relation, target_type, target_id, target_label, evidence_locus, strength, note. It is the only edge file anywhere in these four entries that types BOTH endpoints and carries an explicit strength and a stable edge_id.

The quality_gate_audit block is fully honest on the numeric gates: declared concepts_count 21 / readings_count 5 / aristotle_loci_count 67 / greek_terms_count 32 / tensions_count 6 / ancient_interlocutors_count 10 / modern_interlocutors_count 26 — I counted every array and all seven match exactly.

67 Aristotle loci at Bekker line-pair precision, each with an interpretive role, plus a documented citation-density survey in phase0-overview.md ('~28 occurrences of Physics IV, ~14 of De Memoria, ~9 of De Anima III…').

The scoping rationale is explicitly argued rather than asserted: the manifest and phase0-overview both explain why Bowin was extracted from the Phantasia cluster ('phantasia is the medium of resolution, not the topic in question… misclassifying the chapter would create signal pollution in the Phantasia pipeline's centerpiece-concept analytics'). This is a documented planCorrection of exactly the kind the template asks for.
Bibliographic identification is defended with evidence, not asserted — the venue field records the four independent signals used to confirm the chapter's identity and page range.

Translation provenance is attributed in the unit record (Hussey 1983 for Physics, Sorabji 2004 for De Memoria, with the anchor quotation marked as 'Bowin's translation, slightly modified from Sorabji and Hamlyn').
Zero JSON parse failures, zero ligature corruption, zero mojibake.
entries.verdict: NOT ABANDONED — deliberately scoped, technically the most mature schema in the batch, and permanently unreachable. The brief's characterisation ('FIVE FILES TOTAL, abandoned mid-creation') is wrong on intent and wrong on quality. manifest.json declares "type": "single-article mini-pipeline" with an argued rationale for extracting Bowin from the Phantasia cluster; every numeric gate it sets for itself is met and I verified all seven counts exactly against the arrays; and its edge file is the only one in these four entries that types both endpoints, carries stable edge_ids and resolves 100% of its sources. What it is missing is real, though. It ships no ontology file of any recognised name, which means — uniquely in this batch — it cannot be made reachable by rewriting an existing file; an ontology must be authored. Its one required boolean gate, cross_pipeline_bridge_required, is asserted true against a prose section in phase0-overview.md with no artefact behind it, while both siblings ship actual bridge files. 23 of its 58 edge targets dangle because the interlocutor arrays alone were given no IDs. Its manifest under-declares the type vocabulary by three (UNIT, TENSION, PIPELINE) and the relation vocabulary by two, one of which ('resolved-via') is a one-off misspelling of another ('resolved-by'). It names no source PDF, so 67 Bekker anchors and a page-offset formula float free. And its anchor quotation from De Memoria 450a19-22 sits in the manifest in an unattributed variant that differs from the attributed one in phase0-overview.md:25. Verdict: KEEP AND COMPLETE, and promote its edge schema to the standard for the other three. Completion requires, precisely: (1) a header-format cluster-ontology.md plus .json covering the 21 concepts and 5 readings; (2) IDs on the 10 ancient and 26 modern interlocutors so the 18 interlocutor edges resolve; (3) a real cross-pipeline bridge artefact, with a reciprocal pointer added on the Phantasia side, which currently has none; (4) a source PDF path; (5) a terminology appendix and loci concordance (the 32 Greek terms and 67 loci are already there, they just need the cluster-level file); (6) manifest type/relation vocabularies corrected to the 10 and 15 actually used; and (7) a TEXT_DIRS entry, LAST, after (1). Against the claim/clause target it is the strongest starting point in the batch and the smallest body of work — 1 unit rather than 8 or 12.

=== VERDICTS ON THE PRIOR-AUDIT CLAIMS ===

1. "~310 unit records, 691 unit analyses, ~9,762 distinct edges on disk; ZERO reach runtime." — CONFIRMED for this batch. My four contribute 26 unit records, 26 unit analyses, 1,482 per-source edge rows (506+708+210+58) and 1,422 synthesis rows. compiled-index.json holds 701 ontologyNodes / 72 hooks / 64 tensionEdges; substring counts for 'red dead', 'phantasia secondary', 'emotion secondary', 'motion and time', 'rdr-', 'phx-', 'aes-', 'amt-' are ALL 0.

FILE COUNT CONFIRMED; "abandoned mid-creation" REFUTED. manifest.json declares "type": "single-article mini-pipeline" with an argued extraction rationale, every numeric gate it sets is met (I verified all 7 counts exactly: 21/5/67/32/6/10/26), and it has the BEST edge schema in the batch — the only one typing both endpoints with stable edge_ids and 100% resolvable sources.

=== THINGS THAT SURPRISED ME ===
A. `# dfd… —` is baked into the H1 of 10 of the 11 RDR2 _synthesis markdown files (od -c confirms `d f d` + U+2026). A keyboard-mash placeholder survived the entire build and the quality-gates pass — and it is in the H1 of quality-gates-report.md itself.
B. RDR2's quality-gates-report.md declares non-registration as DESIGN: "it is not part of compiled-index.json by design, and is consumed directly by agents (read as files)." Outside .backups and tmp, the ONLY live file in the repo referencing any of these four entries is plans/secondary-cluster-index-plan-TEMPLATE-2026-07-15.md — a plan document. No script, no service, no runtime component reads them. There is no agent consuming them "directly as files."
C. Edge topology is the real granularity story and it is wildly inconsistent. RDR2: all 12 per-unit files are pure stars (1 distinct source each = the unit) — zero concept-to-concept edges exist in the entry. The compiler reads the .md only. `scripts/compile-corpus-index.py:118-122` registers `"In-Game (Calleja 2011)"` with `ontology_format: "header"`, `analysis_subdir: "_synthesis"`; the header branch at `:1217-1226` opens `analysis_dir / "book-level-ontology.md"` (fallback `cluster-ontology.md`) and nothing else. `grep -n '\.csv' scripts/compile-corpus-index.py` returns NOTHING — no CSV is read anywhere. `book-level-ontology.json` is never opened by the compiler.

5. `_synthesis/concept-matrix.csv` has 46 data rows: C-001…C-038, D-001…D-006, T-001, T-002. No P-xxx row. Correct.

WHAT NEEDS CORRECTING:

(a) "exist only in the JSON twin" is too strong. All 18 are narrated in prose in the .md at `book-level-ontology.md:70` (`## 6. Position consolidation`), with every id P-001…P-018 appearing at lines 72 and 74 with a gloss. Two ids also appear as live edge endpoints in `_synthesis/global-edges.csv` — P-004 at line 141 and P-018 at lines 694, 695, 696, 734, 735, 736, 737. Neither route is machine-readable canonical structure and neither is read by the compiler (prose is not a `#### N.` node; no CSV is read), so the substance survives — but "only in the JSON" is not literally true.

(b) "Every canonical claim-level assertion … is unreachable" overstates by two. §7 of the .md records that the three excisions were lifted into hybrid `POSITION-AS-CONCEPT` concept nodes, and those DO reach runtime: compiled-index has exactly 3 POSITION-AS-CONCEPT nodes, all Calleja — "Magic-circle excision", "Lusory-attitude excision", "Fun-essentialism excision" (C-035/036/037). P-008 (magic circle) and P-009 (fun-essentialism) therefore have content-equivalent runtime twins. 16 of 18, not 18 of 18, are wholly absent.

(c) "the only genuinely claim-level canonical layer this entry has" is wrong as stated. All 13 unit `*-deep.json` files carry their own `positions` arrays totalling 71 records (ig-00:5, ig-01:5, ig-02:5, ig-03:8, ig-04:6, ig-05:5, ig-06:6, ig-07:6, ig-08:6, ig-09:5, ig-10:5, ig-11:6, ig-apx:3). Those are equally unreachable, plus `_synthesis/tension-edges.json` holds 12 tensions that also yield zero runtime edges (compiled-index `tensionEdges` has 64 entries, none from Calleja). The book-level 18 are the *deduplicated canonical* claim layer, not the only claim layer.

(d) SEVERITY: CRITICAL is inflated. This is the uniform §3A registration convention for every companion concept book, not a Calleja-specific breakage. `A Grammar of Motives (Burke 1945)/_synthesis/book-level-ontology.md` has exactly 56 `####` headings against a .json of 56 concepts + 12 positions — 0 positions registered. `Uncomfortable Situations/_synthesis/book-level-ontology.md` has exactly 36 headings against 36 concepts + 18 positions — 0 positions registered. The .md §3A header at line 116 even labels itself "*Auto-generated registration nodes (harvested by scripts/compile-corpus-index.py) from book-level-ontology.json*", i.e. the generator was scoped to concepts+dimensions by design. The runtime schema is not incapable of positions (it already holds `position`, `CLAIM`, and `POSITION-AS-CONCEPT` typed nodes), so this is a fixable systemic scoping gap in the registration convention, not entry corruption. HIGH.

AGAINST THE USER'S CLAIM-LEVEL GOAL: the finding matters more than its severity label suggests. The positions array is the single most claim-shaped canonical structure in this entry — each record is a proposition with a claim string, a primary unit, and supporting units — and it is precisely the layer the stated goal ("every claim and every clause") needs. That 89% of it (16/18) plus 71 unit-level positions never reach runtime is a real and directionally important defect. But it is a system-wide compiler/registration scoping issue to be fixed once across all companion books, not a CRITICAL corruption unique to Calleja.

result.corrected_claim:
The 18 canonical POSITION records in `corpus/index/In-Game (Calleja 2011)/_synthesis/book-level-ontology.json:517` (P-001…P-018, keys canonical_id/claim/tier/primary_unit_id/supporting_units/synonyms_merged) are not registered as nodes and do not reach the runtime index. The §3A registration section of the .md twin (`book-level-ontology.md:114`, self-labelled at line 116 as auto-generated from the .json) emits exactly 44 `#### N.` nodes — 38 concepts + 6 involvement dimensions, lines 118 through 419 — and no positions; `scripts/compile-corpus-index.py:1217-1226` reads only `book-level-ontology.md` for header-format texts and reads no CSV at all (`grep '\.csv'` on the compiler returns nothing), so `corpus/index/compiled-index.json` holds exactly 44 `Calleja - In-Game` nodes. The entry's own `_synthesis/concept-matrix.csv` likewise covers only C-001..C-038, D-001..D-006, T-001..T-002 (46 rows) and omits all P-xxx.

Corrections to the original wording: (1) the positions are not "only in the JSON" — all 18 are glossed in .md prose at lines 70/72/74 and P-004 and P-018 appear as edge endpoints in `_synthesis/global-edges.csv` lines 141 and 694-696/734-737; neither route is machine-readable canonical structure and neither is compiled, so the unreachability conclusion still holds. (2) Not "every" claim reaches nothing: P-008 and P-009 have runtime twins, because the magic-circle and fun-essentialism excisions were lifted into concept nodes C-035/C-037 and appear in compiled-index as `POSITION-AS-CONCEPT`; 16 of 18 are wholly absent, not 18. (3) The positions array is not "the only genuinely claim-level canonical layer" — 13 unit `*-deep.json` files carry 71 further position records and `tension-edges.json` carries 12 tensions, all equally unreachable (compiled-index has zero Calleja tensionEdges of 64).

Severity is HIGH, not CRITICAL: this is the uniform §3A registration convention across every companion concept book, not a Calleja-specific breakage — Burke's `A Grammar of Motives (Burke 1945)/_synthesis/book-level-ontology.md` emits exactly 56 headings for 56 concepts and 0 of its 12 positions, and `Uncomfortable Situations/_synthesis/book-level-ontology.md` emits 36 for 36 concepts and 0 of its 18 positions. The runtime schema already supports position-typed nodes, so this is a one-place scoping gap in the registration generator rather than data corruption. Measured against the claim-level/clause-level goal it is nonetheless the most damaging kind of gap in this entry: the positions array is the only structure here that is genuinely proposition-shaped, and 89% of it plus all 71 unit-level positions are invisible to the runtime.

entries.granularity_gap: Finest structured unit = a FINDING-STRUCTURE, i.e. a whole survey finding (F1-F8) or one lab-record case, collapsed into a single ~60-word `definition` string. That is one level ABOVE chapter granularity in information density, and roughly three levels above clause-level. Nothing in the entry is addressable below the node: no claim IDs, no clause spans, no offsets, no quote-to-claim links. BUT the claim-level material is already authored, in prose, in quantity: vle-04 contains 38 individually numbered, individually page-cited, individually provenance-tagged catalog items (`grep -cE '^[0-9]+\. \*\*\[' → 38`) — that is a claim-level index in markdown-list clothing and would convert to records almost mechanically. vle-03 holds 34 verbatim student quotations, each already keyed to respondent+item (W25-R095/Q9, S25-R022/Q6, …) — that is clause-level evidence with a stable locator scheme, already present. vle-01 holds 8 numbered findings with ~40 embedded statistics. vle-05 holds 6 numbered drafting loci plus 9 [FE-STUDENT] verbatims. Across the entry: 124 quoted strings of ≥25 chars and 57 numbered items in 8,115 words. So the cost of reaching claim level here is NOT authoring — it is schema plus extraction. What would have to be added: (a) a stable per-claim ID namespace distinct from `vle-NN`; (b) a claim record carrying {text, register (FE/FE-U/FE-STUDENT/P), locator (respondent/item or PDF page), status (verified/unverified), supersedes/superseded-by}; (c) exactly the supersession field whose absence causes this entry's worst defect — the ontology and the units disagree on 7 findings and no field records which is current.
strengths: The provenance-register discipline (FE / FE-U / FE-STUDENT / P, plus the O-9 and O-10 consent/processing gates) is applied per-sentence and per-bullet, not per-file. This is the single most valuable thing in the entry and any redesign must keep it as a first-class field, not a prose tag.

vle-03's exemplar bank uses a stable, reconstructible respondent+item locator on every one of 34 verbatims (W25-R095/Q9, W26-R037/Q10). This is already a clause-level addressing scheme; it should become the model for the whole corpus.

vle-04 is a genuine claim-level artefact: 38 numbered items, each with a page, a register, and in most cases the verbatim. It also correctly separates the author's own ideas ([AUTHOR-NOTE] #24) from the source's, which is exactly the discrimination a citation-rigorous index needs.

The entry deliberately refuses duplication: bridge-sources/paper-digest-pointers.md:1 'DO NOT RE-DIGEST' with 6 resolvable pointers into the FCM entry. Every one of those pointers resolves. Single-sourcing was designed in.

vle-00's 'Evidence-weight ledger (standing)' (line 9) grades every channel — 'Lean on ... Corroborating only ... Analogy only' — which is an evidential-strength layer almost nothing else in the corpus has.
manifest.json's declared counts that CAN be checked are correct: ontology_nodes 18 = 18 actual; units array of 6 = 6 files on disk; coding_reliability 0.878 matches vle-01:7.
The cross-instrument keystone is stated once and pointed at (vle-00:11-12), not restated — correct single-source discipline for the corpus's most important claim.
entries.verdict: Salvageable in content, unsound as an index. Judged against its own stated standard the entry is strong: registers are disciplined, the pointer hygiene is real, declared counts check out, and vle-03/vle-04 already carry claim- and clause-level material with stable locators. Judged as an index it is broken at the layer that matters, because the ONE file that reaches runtime — book-level-ontology.md — is the stale layer, and there is no field anywhere that says so. Seven of eighteen runtime nodes carry counts the project superseded on 2026-07-23/24, one carries a reading the author formally retracted on 2026-07-13, and the wrong figure has already leaked into ten live locations in a sibling entry and into compiled-index.json:136. Add to that a source path that resolves nowhere (vle-05, whose four nodes depend on it), a compiler that mangles four node names and injects 'W25' into the greedy-match term list, 42% of the entry's bytes cited by no node, and nine files that no commit contains. Do not rebuild the prose — it is the best empirical writing in the batch. Rebuild the layer: make the units the source of truth, generate the node layer from them, add supersedes/superseded-by and verified/unverified as fields rather than as remarks, and commit the thing.

entries.granularity_gap: Finest structured unit = the cluster concept node — 10 of them across 4 sources, one ~45-word definition each. That is source-level, i.e. two to three levels above claim/clause. The unit .md files sit one notch finer (4 'Key constructs' + 2-3 numbered verbatim loci per source) but are prose. Crucially, claim-level material with explicit epistemic status ALREADY EXISTS here in unstructured form and is unusually well-formed: bridge-to-part-ii.md §3 is a 6-row crosswalk where each row already carries {Lepecq claim, Uexküll anchor, Part II vocabulary, mapping status}, and §7 is an 8-row ledger where each row already carries {claim, layer, status}. That is 14 rows that are, structurally, claim records — they need a schema, not authorship. Add the entry's 8 drafting loci and 15 unit-declared constructs and roughly 37 claim-sized assertions are already written down. Across the entry: 69 quoted strings ≥25 chars and 18 markdown table rows in 6,171 words. What would have to be added to reach the target: (a) stable claim IDs (the entry has NO IDs at any level below ptf-NN — nodes are ordinals, loci are [L1]/[L2] scoped per-file and colliding across files); (b) a verified/unverified field, since the entry already tracks that distinction in prose and gets it wrong once (the three Lepecq bridge quotes); (c) claim→quote→locator links, which citations.md already supplies at source granularity via verified pagination offsets.
strengths: bridge-to-part-ii.md is the best-engineered file in the batch. Its four-layer provenance discipline (FAITHFUL-LEPECQ / FAITHFUL-UEXKÜLL / FAITHFUL-MANTOVANI ****** / ANTICIPATORY-APPLICATION, declared at lines 5-9) is stated before any content and enforced per-row in both tables. §8 'Category caution (honesty)' explicitly refuses the overreach the mapping invites.

Every Von Uexküll cross-reference in the bridge resolves correctly (nodes 2/17/22/27 and 1/3/4, units U-F0/F1/F2/F3/F4 all verified against the target file). Cross-entry citation by node number and unit id actually works here — it is the only place in the batch where a bridge was checked and held.

Pagination offsets are empirically derived and stated as testable propositions, not asserted: citations.md:18 'printed = PDF + 158 (PDF p.1 → head "159"; PDF p.3 → "161"). Verified.' Same at :25 and :32. citations.md:5 also records that archon PageNumber locators are low-trust and were deliberately not used.

The OCR hazard on ptf-01 is caught, named, quantified (pdftotext output = 'Copyright © 1999' × 11), propagated to every downstream file that touches it, and given an explicit remediation instruction (ptf-01:27). This is exactly the failure mode most corpora hide.
concept-matrix.csv is internally consistent with the node layer: all 14 incidence marks were checked against the ten nodes' `units` fields and all 14 agree.

The cluster does real intellectual work rather than summarising: §2 splits the four sources into 'Supports' vs 'Sharpens/complicates' the Part III framing, and ptf-03 is explicitly kept as the counter-weight against the entry's own thesis (ptf-03:36 'both **supports** ... and **complicates** it').
entries.verdict: Sound in substance, structurally incapable of the target, and one bad quotation away from a citation problem. entries.granularity_gap: Finest structured unit = the cluster concept node, 10 across 3 sources, one ~40-word definition each. That is source-level. The prose layer sits finer but is unaddressable: 15 unit-declared 'Key constructs' with centrality+register tags, 8 verified verbatims with page or PDF-page loci, and — the interesting part — a 4-item numbered 'Suggested disposition' (drafting-loci.md:31-40) in which each item is already a claim about how a specific source bears on a specific sentence of the dissertation ('1. Keep the "social interior" phrasing — svw-01 licenses it ontologically; svw-02 instances it empirically'). That is claim-level reasoning already written, keyed to a quoted target passage reproduced verbatim at drafting-loci.md:7-10. Across the entry: 86 quoted strings ≥25 chars in 4,936 words — the highest quotation density per word in the batch. So roughly 27 claim-sized assertions (15 constructs + 8 loci + 4 dispositions) are authored and none is addressable. To reach the target: (a) node and claim IDs (there are none at any level below svw-NN); (b) a claim→source-passage link, which drafting-loci already does in prose; (c) typed edges, since the entry's central intellectual move is a disagreement (svw-03 against the draft's multiplayer equation) that currently exists as a DEBATE-AXIS node with no edge and no tension-edges.json.
strengths: The cluster is built for a purpose and says so: README.md:3-4 and cluster-ontology.md §1 name the exact sentence of the Part III introduction the cluster exists to revise, and reproduce it verbatim at drafting-loci.md:7-10. Every source is then assessed as Confirms / Sharpens / Challenges against that target. This purpose-binding is rare and should survive any redesign.

The entry argues against its own drafting claim rather than supporting it. cluster-ontology.md:43-45 and drafting-loci.md:35-38 both conclude the draft's equation of 'social interior' with multiplayer should be softened, on Champion's evidence. An index that can falsify the prose it serves is doing real work.

Explicit misuse cautions attached to specific sources: cluster-ontology.md:46-47 and drafting-loci.md:39-40 both warn that svw-02 documents a support/creative community and must not be cited as a pedagogical deployment. That is a negative constraint, and negative constraints are exactly what a claim-level index needs and usually lacks.

Pagination offsets derived from running heads and stated testably (citations.md:10 'printed page = PDF page + 386. Verified: PDF p.1 → running head "387"; PDF p.21 → "407"'), plus an explicit refusal to trust archon PageNumber locators (citations.md:5).

The venue-forensics on svw-03 is exemplary: citations.md:22 catches an unfilled ACM template footer ('Conference'04… Copyright 2004 ACM'), identifies it as boilerplate, and fixes the real venue from the paper's own body text, then refuses to invent page numbers (:23).
concept-matrix.csv is fully consistent with the node layer — all 16 incidence marks were checked against the ten nodes' `units` fields and all 16 agree.
entries.verdict: Excellent as a drafting instrument, near-useless as an index, and structurally incapable of the claim-level target. Judged by (a) its own standard — a purpose-built cluster that revises one named sentence — it is the sharpest small entry in the batch: it binds every source to a target passage, it argues against the draft it serves, it attaches negative use-constraints to specific sources, and its venue and pagination forensics are careful. Judged by (b) the claim/clause-level goal it cannot get there without a rebuild, because it has no IDs below svw-NN, no source paths at all, no typed edges, and no way to address the ~27 claim-sized assertions it has already written. The specific defects are moderate rather than fatal — one mis-keyed locus, one core construct dropped from the node layer, one unverifiable ingest-state assertion — with two exceptions that are not the entry's fault but bite it hardest: the compiler mangles four of its ten node names and injects the bare word 'debate' into the greedy-match term list, and all eight files are untracked by git. Keep the prose and the purpose-binding wholesale; replace the node layer with generated records carrying IDs, source paths, and the typed disagreement the entry already states in words.

The unit-level cross-references to vle-01/vle-05 are prose mentions with no path and no edge; the VLE side has no reciprocal reference to riv-01 or riv-02 (verified: `grep -rn 'riv-0' 'corpus/index/Virtual Learning Environments (King–Salvo)'` → 0 hits), so the connection the README calls the entry's 'Part III connection' exists in exactly one direction and in prose only. concept-matrix.csv is an incidence grid (2 data rows, 8 marks); edge_rows_synthesis reports the 2 CSV data rows. entries.granularity_gap: Finest structured unit = the cluster concept node, 7 across 2 sources, one ~35-word definition each. That is source-level and, at 2 sources, barely above entry-level. The prose layer holds 8 unit-declared constructs with centrality+register tags and 6 verified verbatims with loci — roughly 14 claim-sized assertions in 2,832 words (40 quoted strings ≥25 chars). The entry is unusual in that its ANALYTICAL claims are finer-grained than its structural ones: cluster-ontology.md:13-23 argues a two-lever decomposition (Golliher = doing lever, Ulrich = moving lever) and riv-01:44-45 states an operational TEST ('a design is "not fully interactive" when it "does not demand that visitors" act') that is directly checkable against the VLE corpus's A₃→A₄ stall. That test is exactly a claim-level object — it has a source, a verbatim, a locus, and a target it can be run against — and it is encoded as a sentence inside a §5 heading. What would have to be added: (a) IDs at node and locus level (none exist; [L1] already collides across two files); (b) a claim record with {text, source, locus, verification status, target}; (c) a real edge to vle-01/vle-05, which the entry asserts in prose three times and encodes zero times. Being only 2 sources and 7 nodes, this entry is the clearest case in the batch where the current unit of analysis is simply too coarse to be worth a separate entry at all.
strengths: The grouping decision is argued, dated, and traceable to a prior option set rather than assumed: cluster-ontology.md:13-23 gives the rationale in full and closes with '(The Phase-1 proposal offered C1 combined vs. C2 standalone; the reading supports C1.)'. An index that records why two sources were merged is recording a decision most corpora lose.

The two-lever decomposition is real analysis, not summary: Golliher = interactivity→agency (the doing lever), Ulrich = immersion→persuasion (the moving lever), stated identically and consistently at README.md:7-8, cluster-ontology.md:20-21, riv-01:49-50 and riv-02:46-47. Cross-file consistency of the entry's central claim is perfect.

riv-01:44-45 supplies an operational, falsifiable test ('not fully interactive when it does not demand that visitors act') and ties it to a named finding in another entry (the VLE A₃→A₄ stall). This is the entry's highest-value object and the one thing a redesign must preserve as a first-class record.

The Ulrich venue problem is caught, evidenced from three independent signals (missing journal name in extractable text, 'Ulrich 5…17' running heads, Sept–Oct 2011 photo captions), reasoned to a probable answer, and still refused: citations.md:17 'but this is **flagged `****** UNVERIFIED:`** — confirm before citing.' Refusing to close an inference you cannot close is the correct behaviour.

riv-02's pagination offset is two-anchor verified and the offsets are internally consistent with every locus (checked: PDF p.1 + 4 = printed 5; riv-01's PDF 26-28 − 4 = thesis 22-24, PDF 6-8 − 4 = 2-4, PDF 35-37 − 4 = 31-33 — all four arithmetic checks pass).
concept-matrix.csv incidence marks are fully consistent with the node layer: all 8 marks checked against the seven nodes' `units` fields, all 8 agree.
entries.verdict: Sound but sub-scale — this should not be an entry, it should be two source records inside a larger structure. By its own standard the cluster is competent and in two respects better than competent: it argues its grouping decision instead of assuming it, and it refuses to close the Ulrich venue inference it cannot close. But it is 7 files and 2 sources, its entire runtime contribution is 7 concept names, and 5 of those 7 names are mangled by the compiler into a name plus a fake Greek lemma, while 2 of 7 concept-matrix columns already diverge from the node names by Unicode normalisation alone — so the same entry now carries three incompatible spellings of five of its seven concepts, with no IDs to fall back on. It declares no source path at all, hard-codes an admittedly unverified year into its own directory name, and asserts its 'Part III connection' to vle-01/vle-05 three times in prose with zero reciprocal references and zero edges. The content is worth keeping wholesale, especially riv-01's operational A₃→A₄ test. The container is not: at this size the entry-per-cluster layout costs a full _synthesis/ apparatus, a manifest that was never written, and a concept-matrix with two data rows, to deliver seven strings. Fold it into a source-level table with IDs and real edges.

entries.granularity_gap: Finest structured unit = the DATASET-CHANNEL, 7 of them. That is not claim-level at all — it is a level ORTHOGONAL to claims: the entry deliberately holds measurement structure and pushes findings to vle-02 (manifest.json:7 'the study's findings are registered as vle nodes 10-14 there and are NOT duplicated here'). Within its own scope the granularity is actually good: manifest.json:24-32 gives each channel 6-7 typed attributes (id, modality, register, n, unit, status, o9/o10), which is finer than anything else in the batch encodes. But it means BEX contributes essentially ZERO claim-level material by design — bex-01's four load-bearing cases (S03/S04/S05/S07) are the only claim-shaped objects, and they are duplicated verbatim from vle-02:13-16. The batch's claim-level content is elsewhere. The real question this entry raises is different: because it is a channel schema rather than an analysis, 'full treatment' on the cluster template is the wrong target. What it needs is a DATASET record type — channels, cohorts, gates, processing state, provenance register — which the manifest already IS, and which the runtime cannot see. To reach claim level would require lifting bex-01's aggregates (16/24 dilation, 6/8 depletion, boredom means 7.0/6.0/4.5) into records; but doing that here would violate the entry's own no-duplication rule, so the right move is to make vle-02's findings claim-level and leave BEX as the dataset descriptor it correctly is.
strengths: Deliberate anti-duplication, stated as a rule and actually enforced: manifest.json:7 and book-level-ontology.md:8-9 both declare findings live at vle-02 and are not repeated; bridge-sources/paper-digest-pointers.md:1 'DO NOT RE-DIGEST'. All 5 pointers resolve. This is the cleanest single-sourcing discipline in the batch.

The gates are explicit, named, and machine-readable: manifest.json:42-46 gives a 3-key gates object (PII / O-10 / O-9) with a stated scope for each, and every unit restates the relevant gate. bex-00:19-21 records that the raw person-named Subjects/ directory was deliberately NOT enumerated. A corpus that records what it refused to read is unusual and valuable.

Cohort-N heterogeneity is treated as a first-class hazard rather than smoothed over: manifest.json:17-23 gives three distinct N's with an explicit warning note, and bex-00:40-42, bex-02:17-19, bex-03:13-15 each independently restate 'a published-channel derivation is not the same cohort as the raw N=8'. Three chances to catch the error a reader would otherwise make.

Processing state is tracked per channel with a work breakdown and a file-verified plan: manifest.json:47-52 distinguishes 'currently_usable' from deferred, estimates effort ('light CPU'), and points at plans/boredom-experiment-o9-processing-scope-2026-07-16.md, which exists. Knowing what has NOT been processed is as important as knowing what has.

A prior factual error was found and corrected in place with a date and a consequence: manifest.json:29 and ontology:77 both record that ch-obs is 'OBS screen-capture of the subject's first-person in-VR view ... NOT a body/comportment camera: no participant body footage was ever recorded (confirmed 2026-07-16), so posture/fidget/watch-glance are not recoverable and there is no independent third behavioral surface.' The correction propagates the analytic consequence, not just the fact.
It is the only entry in the batch under version control (9/9 files tracked), and the only one whose every testable declared path resolves.
entries.verdict: Sound for what it is, mis-scoped as an 'entry', and the clearest case in the batch that the container is the problem rather than the content. This is not a cluster of sources and it is not an analysis — it is a dataset descriptor, and as a dataset descriptor it is the best-engineered artefact here: seven channels with typed attributes, three explicit gates, three cohort-N warnings restated in three places, per-channel processing state with a file-verified plan, and a corrected factual error whose analytic consequence is propagated. All seven of its testable in-repo paths resolve and it is the only entry anyone committed. The defects are mostly the consequence of forcing dataset metadata through a concept-ontology template: 7 channels compressed into 5 unit files so three channels have no address, a channels[].n field carrying four types, a .mmd whose 15 arrows include 3 self-loop annotation hacks and an orphan note node, and a 'peripheral' centrality tier invented for one node. The one substantive content error is that bex-00:6 says five measurement channels where its own table two paragraphs later says seven. The one substantive integration error is not BEX's fault: six live locations in the sibling VR Pedagogy Secondary entry still assert this entry does not exist, and ped-sec-01's .json and .md flatly contradict each other about the same bridge. Do not rebuild it. Give it a DATASET record type, promote the manifest to the thing that reaches runtime, and fix the six stale sibling assertions.

(1) COMPILER CORRUPTION — 16 of these 52 nodes (31%) have their name truncated and the parenthetical mis-filed into the Greek-lemma field, which then enters canonicalTerms as a greedy-match term. The differential is the outlier among the three synthesis files.

WHERE THE ORIGINAL CLAIM IS WRONG — the consequence understates the damage. It says the refuted claim is "positioned to flow straight into Part II prose." It has ALREADY flowed. `tmp/Dissertation/Part_II/Part-II-COMBINED-v2-2026-07-01.tex:521`: "The bear charges (clip 9, 11:00): the image lunges at the screen, and the player's body pulls back. That is a forward-looking to-do, not a correction pointer; it is dated the same day as the verification log so a reader cannot tell it predates the refutation; and the manifest's `"status": "done"` cancels it. I could not refute the claim; every load-bearing assertion held under direct inspection, and two of the failure modes I was told to hunt for turned out to cut in the claim's favour rather than against it.

Line numbers are exact, not off-by-one: an AST parse puts the TEXT_DIRS literal at lineno 35, end_lineno 133 — precisely the cited range. The dict genuinely lacks any RDR2 key. Critically, I confirmed there is no alternate ingestion path: CORPUS_INDEX is dereferenced at only three sites, two of which iterate TEXT_DIRS and one of which hardcodes the Aristotle directory. No generic glob exists, so "the compiler never opens any of its 60 files" is structurally guaranteed rather than merely observed. The compiled index itself contains zero byte-level traces of the entry, and the file-count denominator is clean (find with and without the .backups exclusion both return 60).

The most promising refutation was the design-decision defense, which the entry states in its own words at quality-gates-report.md:26-27: secondary-literature clusters are "not part of compiled-index.json by design." Had that held, this would be a design decision mistaken for a defect. It does not hold. The ruling is dated 2026-06-23, and git -S searches show five sibling secondary clusters — all using the identical _synthesis/cluster-ontology.md shape, none having a book-level-ontology.md — were wired into TEXT_DIRS on 2026-07-15 and 2026-07-16, with commit messages that literally say "compiler wiring." The project's own practice reversed the policy three weeks later and never revisited this entry. The compiler's comment at :1219 naming "RDR2 Secondary" among clusters using cluster-ontology.md, sitting inside a branch that only runs for registered directories, is the author asserting a wiring that does not exist. I also ruled out staleness: the entry's files predate the last index build by 27 days.

Two things in the original claim are wrong, but neither rescues it. First, TEXT_DIRS holds 19 keys, not 20 — a trivial miscount that does not touch the conclusion. Second, and more substantively, the stated consequence mis-attributes causation: the compiler imports no csv module and globs only two markdown patterns, so the 506 edges and 12 unit JSONs are unreachable for every entry, registered or not — Boredom Secondary's 1,897 edges are equally absent. The edges are indeed invisible, but not because of the TEXT_DIRS omission. What the omission actually costs is the cluster's ontology nodes and canonical terms.

Against that, I found an aggravator the original agent missed, which is why I did not downgrade severity. Registering the entry would not fix it. parse_header_ontology splits on ^####\s+\d+\. or ^\*\*\d+\., and the entry's 47-line cluster-ontology.md contains zero of either — so it would yield zero nodes, and would do so silently, because the only guard is a file-existence check that passes. The same non-conforming shape appears in the two other unregistered secondary clusters. The fix is therefore a reformat plus a registration, not the one-line addition the claim implies. Combined with the entry being entirely untracked in git, and with the user's goal of actually leveraging this index, total invisibility of a complete 12-article cluster warrants keeping CRITICAL. Worth noting for calibration: this entry cleanly passes the layer-disagreement check the prior audit flagged elsewhere — its per-source CSVs sum to exactly the 506 rows in global-edges.csv.

THE OBSERVED FACT IS CONFIRMED EXACTLY — I could not refute it.

All 12 per-unit edge CSVs parse (csv.DictReader, quote-aware) to exactly 1 distinct `source` value, and that value is the unit's own ID. Row counts and the two spot-checks in the finding's evidence are correct to the row, with no off-by-one and no .backups contamination (`find ... -path '*.backups*'` returns nothing inside this entry — the entry has no snapshot dirs at all). Union of all `source` values across the 12 files = 12; union of all `target` values = 487; the intersection targets∩sources is EMPTY, so the edge layer has depth exactly 1. 506 per-unit rows = 506 global-edges.csv rows = manifest.json:36 `"global_edges": 506`. So "star graph, zero concept-to-concept edges in the CSV edge layer" is true as written.

BUT TWO OF THE ENUMERATED FAILURE MODES APPLY, and they gut the stated consequence.

(1) "A consequence that does not actually follow from the observed fact." The consequence's first clause — "No path exists between any two concepts" — is FALSE, and demonstrably so. A star is not a set of isolated nodes; every pair of concepts attached to the same hub is at distance 2. I built the undirected graph from all 506 rows: 499 nodes in 10 connected components of sizes 128, 69, 59, 45, 41, 40, 39, 33, 32, 13. BFS gives dist('procedural rhetoric (Bogost)' → 'honor gauge as procedural argument') = 2, and a CROSS-UNIT path of length 4 from rdr-03's 'ideological state apparatus (ISA)' to rdr-07's 'nature representation as multimodal construction' — because three targets collide across units and fuse rdr-03+rdr-04+rdr-07 into one 128-node component (rdr-03-tuominen-edges.csv:39 and rdr-07-ventomaki-edges.csv:45 both target "honor system"; rdr-03-tuominen-edges.csv:28 and rdr-04-crowley-edges.csv:21 both target "Humphreys (2012)"). Co-occurrence traversal is exactly what a bipartite incidence layer provides, and it works here.

The second clause — "no debate reconstruction" — is also FALSE, twice over. (a) At entry level, _synthesis/debate-map.json holds 10 debates (D1–D10), each with an `axis` and 4–5 `positions` carrying `{unit, stance}`, e.g. D3 "Is player agency meaningful, illusory, or foreclosed?" with five per-unit stances; _synthesis/contested-readings.md is its prose twin and _synthesis/concept-matrix.csv is a 24-concept × 12-unit incidence matrix. (2) "Mistaking a design decision for a defect." The `source` column is an ATTRIBUTION column by construction, not a graph tail — it records which article asserts the row. manifest.json:5 declares the schema is copied from "corpus/index/Aristotelian Phantasia Secondary (1985-2017)". The entry never claims a concept-to-concept graph and in fact says the opposite in two places: _synthesis/citation-network.json:14 ("debate-map.json + rdr-game-element-concordance.json (not a citation graph) are what make this a cluster") and _synthesis/quality-gates-report.md:18 ("The debate-map and concordance (not a citation graph) are what make this a cluster"). Its own gate was a VOLUME gate — quality-gates-report.md:8 "| Global edges | ≥220 | **506** | ✓ |" — never a topology gate. By standard (a), its own template, the entry passes.

WHERE THE FINDING KEEPS REAL FORCE — standard (b), the claim/clause-level target. The 487 targets are uncontrolled free text with no node IDs: only 3 exact-string collisions across all 12 units (0.6% of 506 rows), and normalizing case/punctuation adds nothing (still 3). Unit JSONs hold concept-vs-concept material only as PROSE — rdr-03-tuominen.json `tensions` are strings like "Real mechanical player agency (honor, 'freedom') vs. fixed narrative outcomes…" — never as parsed relations. The five .mmd files contribute only 41 arrow-lines total and just four concept→chain arrows (rdr-graph-cross-pipeline-bridge.mmd:17,20,21,22). So the entry genuinely cannot carry claim-level or clause-level connection structure without a separate vocabulary-normalization pass. That is a real limitation — but it is a limitation against the user's future target, not a broken graph, and it does not stop traversal or debate reconstruction today.

VERDICT: defect real, evidence numerically exact, but the stated consequence is wrong on its two load-bearing clauses and the severity is inflated by them. HIGH → MEDIUM.

## 4. Cross-entry patterns

**Systemic — a property of the pipeline, not of any author:**

1. **Runtime blindness.** Every entry authors 20–100× more structure than the compiler can see. This is a property of `scripts/compile-corpus-index.py`, and no amount of authoring care changes it. It is the root cause of ~40% of all filed defects.
2. **Dual serialization with no declared authority.** 15 entries maintain both a per-source and a synthesis edge layer. **Not one** declares which wins in a machine-readable field. Only Grammar documents its delta. Four entries disagree for four different reasons.
3. **Correction can never reach the artifact it corrects, because rows have no IDs.** This is the single most damaging recurring pattern and it is invariant across media. RDR2 Playthrough (prose beat rows), Veri(dis)similitude (prose matrix rows), VR Pedagogy (`citation-corrections-2026-07-16.md`), Aristotle (the offset fix applied to prose and not to JSON), Boredom Secondary (`contested-readings.md` CR-12a/b/c cited but never defined). In every case the correction was written as a *new document* because there was no addressable row to edit. Add IDs without adding a `supersedes` edge and this will recur.
4. **Summary blocks contradict the data in the same file.** In-Game: `ig-bibliography-extracted.json:24,267,269,271` gives four incompatible counts; `ig-interlocutor-map.json:815-822` says 66 for a 73-element array; `ig-terminology-appendix.json:154` says 132 for 141. Uncomfortable: `book-level-ontology.json:17-21`. Boredom Secondary: `cluster-ontology.md:135` (TERM 24 vs 25, DEBATE-AXIS 12 vs 8, METHOD omitted — the two errors cancel so any total-only check passes). Grammar: 6 of 14 units mis-report their own edge count. A Rhetoric of Motives: 6 of 8.
5. **Phase-ordering artifacts frozen into data.** Debate-axis IDs (`DA-NN`) are a Phase-3B deliverable; edges are Phase-2. Result: **zero of 260 `shifts-debate-axis` rows corpus-wide begin with an ID token** — Boredom 56 rows/46 spellings, VR Pedagogy 40/21, RDR2 22/22, Phantasia 11/1, AES 1/1. The vocabulary exists; it simply post-dates its consumers.
6. **`/tmp` as an evidence store.** In-Game (6 paths), Uncomfortable (2), Game-Behavior (1, destroyed), RDR2 Playthrough (65 references), Veri(dis)similitude (1). Every one is gone. The pattern correlates with the finest-grained evidence in each entry.
7. **German written into a field named `greek`** (259 of 448 populated values), and node names truncated at parentheses. Both are parser-contract mismatches nobody could see from inside an entry.

**One-off:**
- The Aristotle offset abandonment (a single interrupted repair, reconstructible from mtimes).
- `ig-10-incorporation.json:155` (one character).
- The RDR2 U+00D7 path (one character, two lines).
- Grammar's 398-value relation vocabulary — one entry, one decision not to declare a closed set.

**Outliers, and why:**
- **Dissertation** — indexes the user's *own* prose, not a source. Has the finest granularity in the corpus (1 claim per 58 words) and the best provenance apparatus (sha256+bytes+lines+words per input, with prior-run deltas), and is registered nowhere. Its 273 `.md` are in ChromaDB and its 69 `.json` are not — the exact inversion of what should be true.
- **Game-Behavior Analysis Method** — not an index at all. It is the *instrument*. 11 structured records for 82,134 words. Its correct role in a redesign is as the controlled vocabulary (R1–R7, A0–A4, the 6×6 Burke×Calleja grid), not as an entry.
- **A Rhetoric of Motives** — the only entry that declared a closed relation vocabulary and a binary provenance rule *before* authoring, and honoured both. 420 edges, 10 relations, 0 singletons, 0 empty cells, 0 duplicate triples. It ships half the apparatus of its sibling Grammar and is structurally healthier for it.
- **Aristotelian Motion and Time Secondary** — 5 files, 1 unit. An abandoned stub with a manifest.
- **The six Part III "lite" entries** (Boredom Experiment, Presence Theory, Rhetoric of Interactivity, Social Presence, VLE, plus Veri(dis)similitude) — md-only, 7–10 files, no unit JSON, no edges. Five are registered and contribute 52 runtime nodes on 25,203 words. They are the cheapest nodes-per-hour in the corpus and the least able to support anything below concept level.

## 5. What is genuinely excellent

These are the artifacts that ~40 hours per entry actually bought. A redesign must carry them forward **verbatim**; they are the expensive part and the hardest to reproduce.

**Provenance discipline — the single most valuable invention in the corpus.**
The three-way tag `FE` (the source's own published claim) / `FAITHFUL-<author>` (close paraphrase of a specific passage) / `P-anticipatory-application` (the project's own interpretive link, never the source's). Corpus-wide: **1,107 FE tags, 1,265 FAITHFUL tags, 922 anticipatory-application tags**. The rule is written down at `corpus/index/Boredom Secondary (Part III)/bridge-sources/anchor-pointers.md:157-161`. ### 6.4 The multiplier — arithmetic from observed data

**Source corpus actually indexed.** The five primary source directories hold **18,557 PDF pages across 210 documents** (`rhetorical_ontology` 10,296 / 63 · `new_media` 3,108 / 43 · `boredom` 3,572 / 50 · `metaphysics` 943 / 19 · `pedagogy` 638 / 35). The index covers roughly 130 of those documents: ~12 monographs (Aristotle 553 verified, Grammar 551 verified, BT ~490, RM 356, FCM ~370, BCAP ~340, Rickert ~300, H&R ~250, Uncomfortable ~230, Uexkull ~230, In-Game ~200, Wendt ~200 ≈ **4,070 pp.**) plus ~118 articles (Boredom 50, VR Pedagogy 34, RDR2 Sec 12, Phantasia 8, AES 5, AMT 1, Part III lite 15, at ~20 pp. avg ≈ **2,530 pp.**). **≈ 6,600 indexed source pages ≈ 2.64 M source words** at ~400 words/page.

**Claims.** Two independent estimators:
- *Observed density.* Dissertation achieved 982 claims over 56,713 words = **1 claim / 58 words**. Veri(dis)similitude: 157 / 15,481 = 1 / 99. Applying 1/58–1/99 to 2.64 M words → **26,700 – 45,500 claims.**
- *Per-page.* 3–5 substantive propositions per page × 6,600 pages → **20,000 – 33,000 claims.**

Converging range: **≈ 25,000 – 40,000 claims.**

**Clauses.** 2.64 M source words ÷ 12–18 words per clause → **147,000 – 220,000 clauses.** Cross-check from Aristotle alone: 2,323 distinct Bekker line-loci are already recorded in prose for 553 pages = 4.2 clause-addresses per page; extrapolated at that (very conservative, since it counts only *cited* lines) → 27,700; the true clause count for Aristotle's 553 pages at ~23 clauses/page is ~12,700 for that entry alone.

**Multipliers against today:**

| Layer | Today | Complete | Multiplier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Addressable units | 362 | 362 | 1× |
| Claim records | 2,615 (of which 0 at runtime) | 25,000 – 40,000 | **10× – 15×** on structure; **∞** on runtime |
| Clause records | 0 | 147,000 – 220,000 | **new layer** |
| Edges | 9,702 unit-to-string | claim-to-claim at ~2–3 per claim | **50,000 – 120,000** |
| Runtime records | 701 nodes + 72 hooks + 64 tensions = 837 | ≥ 200,000 | **≈ 240×** |

Two thirds of the claim work is already *written*: ~14,000 tagged prose assertions + 2,615 structured records ≈ 16,600 of a 25,000–40,000 target, i.e. **40–66% of the claim layer already exists as text**. What does not exist at all is the clause layer and any addressing scheme below the page.

### 6.5 Foundation or obstacle — the plain answer

**The scholarship is a foundation. The format is an obstacle. The registration path is a wall.**

Three specific structural properties make the current format incapable of the goal, and none of them is fixable by authoring more entries the same way:

1. **The finest locator in the entire corpus is a page number.** Nothing on disk carries a sentence offset, a character span, or a bbox. Where sub-page anchors were attempted (In-Game's 995 line-ranges), they pointed into a `/tmp` file that no longer exists. Aristotle's Bekker line numbers are the one genuine exception, and they live in markdown bullets under 30 different heading conventions.
2. **The edge model cannot express a claim-to-claim relation.** Every one of the 9,702 edges is keyed on `(source, relation, target)` where both endpoints are unit IDs or free-text strings, with `locus` as an unindexed note column. At claim granularity, endpoint collisions become the norm — and `corpus/index/Boredom Secondary (Part III)/_synthesis/global-edges.csv` already demonstrates what happens: a dedup key of `(s,r,t)` destroyed the `locus` and `note` of 21 rows, 12 of them the passage-level Heidegger bridges that are the entry's most valuable data. **The synthesis step deletes exactly the evidence the goal requires**, and it will delete more of it the deeper the index goes.
3. **There is no runtime slot for a claim, a tension, an edge, a quotation or a locus.** `compiled-index.json` has four arrays and none of them is any of those. Adding 40,000 claims to the current format produces 40,000 records that reach nothing, at the current 2.61% read surface.

The corrective is not a rebuild. It is: keep every reading, position, claim, locus, provenance tag, correction ledger, offset table and cite-check verbatim; replace the *serialization* (one unit-JSON schema, one edge dialect, one ID namespace, one locus vocabulary extending to character spans); replace the *edge model* (claim-to-claim endpoints, five-column identity, no lossy dedup); and replace the *registration path* (read the JSON that 12 entries already ship, not one markdown section).

## 7. The ten things that must be true before any entry is authored again

**1. Every file is in git before the first byte of analysis is written.**
*Evidence:* 24 of 27 entries — 1,433 files, ~30 MB, including all of Aristotle, Burke, Heidegger and Dissertation — are untracked and not gitignored (`git ls-files corpus/index` returns 326 paths). There is no history, no diff, no recovery, and no way to tell an authored correction from an accidental overwrite. Every other item on this list is worthless if the bytes can vanish.

**2. The registration path is proven end-to-end before authoring, with a JSON reader.**
*Evidence:* the compiler opens 48 of 1,759 files (2.61% of bytes), has zero CSV and zero mermaid support, and hardcodes cross-pipeline hooks to one directory (`scripts/compile-corpus-index.py:1239`). 12 entries ship a clean ontology JSON that nothing reads while the markdown twin is parsed and corrupts 259 `greek` fields and 4 node boundaries. An entry that cannot demonstrate a record round-tripping to `compiled-index.json` on day one will not have one on day 400.

**3. Every addressable object has a globally-unique, prefixed, immutable ID — including claims, edges, tensions and quotations.**
*Evidence:* reading IDs `C1..C19` collide across 6 Boredom Secondary units; Uncomfortable Situations carries four incompatible namespaces for one concept set with zero overlap; compiled nodes have **no `id` field at all**; and the entire one-directional-correction failure (RDR2, Veri(dis), Aristotle, VR Pedagogy) traces to rows that cannot be addressed, so corrections could only be written as new documents that the corrected files never reference.

**4. A `supersedes` / `superseded_by` edge exists and is mandatory for any correction.**
*Evidence:* `corpus/index/Red Dead Redemption 2 (Salvo Playthrough)/frame-read-verification.md:23,:29` claims to correct two beat-maps; **zero of 22 beat-maps contain the string "frame-read-verification"**. Five refuted claims sit live in the entry's highest-retrieval chunks including a §8 summary paragraph. `corpus/index/Veri(dis)similitude (Salvo MA)/gg-e7-dense-trace.md:3` declares it supersedes `gg-frame-trace.md`; that file contains zero hits for "dense", and three files still certify the refuted reading as "confirmed".

**5. Controlled vocabularies are declared in a machine-readable spec BEFORE authoring, and validated after.**
*Evidence:* `corpus/index/A Rhetoric of Motives (Burke 1950)/_synthesis/phase0-overview.md` declared 10 relations and a binary provenance rule in advance — result: 420 edges, 10 relations, zero singletons, zero empty cells. Grammar did not — result: **398 relations for 878 edges**. Same pipeline family, same month. Corpus-wide: 633 relations, 162 `stance` values over 463 readings, 46 free-text spellings for 11 debate axes, and zero of 260 `shifts-debate-axis` rows using an axis ID.

**6. One unit-record schema and one edge dialect, enforced by a validator that runs on commit.**
*Evidence:* **146 distinct unit-JSON key signatures** and **44 edge-CSV header dialects** for 27 entries. `readings` alone takes 8 incompatible sub-shapes inside one entry; three interchangeable locus keys; five column-count variants inside Grammar. 46 ragged rows exist because no validator ever ran, and 12 of them were "repaired" by truncation into the synthesis layer where they now parse cleanly and carry wrong values.

**7. No derived layer may be lossy, and every derived file must record its generator command and its source-layer hash.**
*Evidence:* four dual-layer entries disagree for four different reasons and only one documents its delta. Boredom Secondary's dedup destroyed `locus`+`note` on 21 rows; VR Pedagogy's "dedup" removed 2 rows that were not duplicates and truncated 12 notes; Uncomfortable's ID merge created 12 self-loops; FCM's synthesis layer is a *superset* nobody flagged. Grammar's `_synthesis/canonical-id-resolution-report.md:33-37` is the only honest record and should be the template.

**8. Every locus resolves to a character span in an archived, hash-verified extraction — never to `/tmp` and never to a page alone.**
*Evidence:* In-Game's 995 line-anchors, Uncomfortable's two derived appendices, Game-Behavior's validation transcript, RDR2's 65 frame-log references and Veri(dis)'s 2 fps frame archive all point into deleted scratch space. Meanwhile Uncomfortable Situations survived intact **because it used only page anchors under one declared offset rule** — proof that durable addressing is a choice. Also: `corpus/index/Aristotle - Complete Works/aristotle-bekker-index.json` has 101 of 188 loci wrong by >2 pages because a superseded arithmetic was never re-run, while the correct formula sat three files away in `phase05-offset-validation.md`.

**9. Every quotation is a first-class object with its own page, its own span, and a verified flag — one tag may not cover four quotations.**
*Evidence:* 25,825 quoted spans of ≥25 characters exist across the index; almost none is individually addressable. `corpus/index/VR Pedagogy Secondary (Part III)/Biocca…/ped-sec-29-…md:7` presents a conflated phrase as verbatim with an FE tag, and it survived because one paragraph-terminal `(FAITHFUL-X, p.461-465)` tag covered four distinct quotations. `corpus/index/Dissertation/…/master-citation-report-parsed.json:176` silently drops a parenthetical from a White 1985 verbatim; `:221` ships pdfium ligature loss ("fgures") in a quotation marked for in-text use. Three entries deliberately deleted the clause text under a content filter and can never support clause-level indexing until that is reversed.

**10. A machine-readable gate report is a deliverable, and every declared count is computed, never typed.**
*Evidence:* 2 of 27 entries have a gate report; 2 have a render validation. Where inline gates exist they pass on wrong numbers (`DISS-01-A0/phase2-claims.json:1798`, off by 45; `gm-01-deep.json:339`, certifying compliance its own twin breaches 31 times). Hand-typed summary blocks are wrong in at least 9 entries — In-Game's bibliography gives four incompatible counts of itself; Boredom Secondary's `cluster-ontology.md:135` gets two of five node-type figures wrong in a way that cancels so any total-only check passes; Veri(dis)similitude has 3 of 5 manifest counts wrong. Note also what a gate must *not* be: `RDR2 Secondary`'s `synthesis_files: 22` is correct and certifies nothing — a cluster could pass it with 22 empty files. Gates must measure content, not cardinality.
